headline: Pakistan achieves milestone with successful test of indigenous Fa’az air-to-air missile
description: Pakistan has successfully conducted the flight test of its first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile, marking another significant milestone in the
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan has successfully conducted the flight test of its first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile, marking another significant milestone in the advancement of the country’s aerospace and defence capabilities.

Equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system, the missile is capable of engaging enemy aerial targets at extended ranges, said a news release issued by Inter Services Public Relations (ISPR).

Fa’az will significantly enhance the operational flexibility of the Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country’s overall defense posture. The successful flight test underscores the technical maturity, innovation, and self-reliance achieved by Pakistan’s defense industry.

The launch was witnessed by senior officers of the Pakistan Armed Forces, along with distinguished scientists and engineers who played a pivotal role in the development of this advanced weapon system.

The President, Prime Minister of Pakistan, COAS & CDF, and Services Chiefs have congratulated the scientists and engineers on this remarkable achievement, the news release said.

headline: Pakistan secures 11 China education deals for youth skills
description: The agreements, signed or witnessed by the PMYP chairman, establish cooperation between Pakistani and Chinese institutions in mechatronics, green energy,
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan has secured 11 cooperation agreements and 14 skills and education projects with Chinese institutions during Prime Minister’s Youth Programme (PMYP) Chairman Rana Mashhood Ahmad Khan’s October 27 to November 3 visit to China, aimed at expanding international qualifications, technical training and employment opportunities for Pakistani youth, with Pakistan recording the highest number of signings among participating countries at the 27th China Annual Conference and Expo for International Education (CACIE 2026), according to a press release received here. The agreements, signed or witnessed by the PMYP chairman, establish cooperation between Pakistani and Chinese institutions in mechatronics, green energy, mobile communications, nursing, modern agriculture, cross-border e-commerce and international skills certification.

Of the 11 agreements, PMYP is directly a party to three, signed with the China Global Professional and Technical Certification Center, Jilin Electronic Information Vocational and Technical College, and Peili Vocational College.

The remaining eight involve the University of Lahore, Ghazi University, NUTECH Karachi, Preston Institute of Management Science and Technology, and Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority (TEVTA), in partnership with Chinese vocational institutions.

The visit also saw the unveiling or witnessing of 14 flagship skills and education initiatives, including an International Nursing Talent Training Base, a Cross-Border E-Commerce Talent Training Base unveiled by Rana Mashhood, Pakistan Tiangong College, a Joint Teacher Training Centre, and new committees on Industrial Robotics and Electronic Information Engineering.

In a significant development for employment opportunities linked to the country’s railway infrastructure, China Railway Group Secretary Han Hui flew to Pakistan on the same day following strategic discussions with the PMYP chairman to initiate on-the-ground work on skills training and employment opportunities associated with the Main Line-I (ML-1) railway upgrade.

Under the academic cooperation arrangements, Jilin Electronic Information Vocational and Technical College has already trained 10 Pakistani faculty members and will enrol 15 Pakistani students in its Chinese language programme from November.

“Every student enrolled, and every teacher trained is a step towards a stronger, more skilled Pakistan,” Rana Mashhood said.

The chairman also co-launched the International Green Power Talent Development Base in collaboration with the China Electricity Council, Thailand’s Office of the Vocational Education Commission (OVEC) and TANG International Education Group, aimed at strengthening international cooperation in green energy skills development.

During the visit, he addressed the Belt and Road International Forum on Industry-Education Cooperation, emphasising the need to align vocational training with industry requirements, promote joint academic programmes, introduce internationally recognised certifications and strengthen vocational teacher training.

He also addressed the International Seminar on Green Energy Talent Exchange at the China Electricity Council and held meetings with Pakistan’s Ambassador to China Ali Asad Gillani and senior embassy officials to discuss diplomatic support for education and skills partnerships.

In a separate meeting, Rana Mashhood held discussions with Mrs Benjawan Pokpong, Director of the Bureau of Cooperation at Thailand’s OVEC, on expanding education and vocational training collaboration among Belt and Road partner countries.

As part of the visit, the chairman presented the China-Pakistan International Education Cooperation Awards (2025-2026) under the auspices of the Embassy of Pakistan in Beijing.

To ensure effective implementation of the agreements and projects, the PMYP China Secretariat has been established at the Beijing headquarters of TANG International Education Group. It will coordinate cooperation among government departments, educational institutions and industry partners.

Rana Mashhood said youth empowerment remained a key priority of the government under the leadership of Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, with the initiatives advancing the vision of a Skilled, Empowered and Digital Pakistan.

headline: Petrol price cut by Rs5.45 per litre, diesel rate increased by Rs3.68
description: The federal government has lowered the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre but raised the rate of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68 for the latest pricing
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government has lowered the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre but raised the rate of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68 for the latest pricing period, according to an official notification issued on Tuesday.

Under the revised rates, petrol will now cost Rs369.06 per litre, compared with the previous Rs374.51. The price of high-speed diesel has been increased from Rs391.52 to Rs395.20 per litre.

The new prices will come into force at midnight on November 4 and remain effective until the next review.

The adjustment offers some relief to users of petrol-powered vehicles, including motorcycles and cars, while increasing fuel expenses for diesel consumers. The higher diesel rate may also add to operating costs for transport and logistics businesses, as HSD is commonly used by buses, trucks, heavy vehicles and agricultural machinery. Any rise in transportation expenses could put further pressure on the prices of essential goods.

The revision comes amid government efforts to address the financial difficulties faced by consumers. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said earlier on Tuesday that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed relevant authorities to prepare a winter gas supply plan and take measures to protect vulnerable segments of society.

Speaking at a press conference, Tarar said the government was mindful of the financial challenges facing ordinary citizens. He added that Rs15 billion in refinery profits had been transferred to the public and that profiteering by certain operators in the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector had been curbed.

Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said Pakistan had been facing economic pressures linked to the conflict that began on February 28. He noted that international oil prices had declined and expressed hope that the global market trend would lead to further relief for consumers.

headline: China shows how culture, digital economy can work together: WIPO chief
description: BEIJING - China can be an example of how to combine the creative economy, cultural heritage and the digital economy, Daren Tang, head of the UN’s World
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: BEIJING - China can be an example of how to combine the creative economy, cultural heritage and the digital economy, Daren Tang, head of the UN’s World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO), said a group of journalists. Tang spoke on the sidelines of the 2026 International Copyright Forum, which runs from November 2 to 4 in Dunhuang, Gansu province, northwest China and is co-hosted by China’s National Copyright Administration and WIPO. According to the administration, China’s copyright industry generated 10.06 trillion yuan in value added in 2024, or 7.46 percent of GDP, and employed 15.8 million people in urban units. Tang cited a presentation by Chinese tech giant Tencent on using its digital platforms to promote Chinese culture overseas through films, music and stories. He also pointed to Black Myth: Wukong, a Chinese action game based on the classic novel Journey to the West, which he said introduces international audiences to Chinese culture, history and historical sites, a wire service reported. Worldwide, he said, the creative economy, cultural heritage and digital technologies are coming together to entertain audiences and create economic opportunities, in what he called “the next evolution of the creative economy.” Dunhuang is home to the Mogao Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage site spanning over 1,000 years of Buddhist art. Since 2016, the Dunhuang Academy’s Digital Dunhuang project has offered high-definition images and panoramic tours of 30 caves online worldwide. “Even though there are millions of people who visit Dunhuang, I believe that the whole world deserves to see Dunhuang,” Tang said, calling the project a great example of bringing culture to the world. More than a thousand years ago, people from Europe, the Middle East, Persia, Central Asia and China met and traded in Dunhuang, a stop on the ancient Silk Road. Cultures need such exchange to stay vibrant, Tang said, and copyright helps them preserve their identity while giving creators the confidence to protect their ideas and earn a living from them. He also sees artificial intelligence (AI) as an opportunity, citing a short film by a self-taught Chinese creator that went viral overseas within four days. But AI can also create “a single monoculture,” he said, so it must be trained on diverse cultures. “The role of technology must be to empower, enable, and to support the human creator,” Tang said, adding that the human creator must remain at the center of the copyright system.

headline: Lahore records 15pc improvement in air quality: EPCCD
description: LAHORE - The provincial capital recorded a 15 per cent net improvement across six major air pollutants during the first year of the Punjab government’s
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The provincial capital recorded a 15 per cent net improvement across six major air pollutants during the first year of the Punjab government’s real-time air quality monitoring program, while the city’s peak Air Quality Index (AQI) declined by 28pc in October 2026 compared to the corresponding period last year, according to a report released by the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department (EPCCD). The department said the improvement reflected a reduction across six major atmospheric pollutants rather than a change in a single parameter, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5). Lahore also recorded no days in the hazardous AQI category, defined as an index above 300, during October 2026,against four such days in October 2025. The findings were based on the first full year of real-time air quality monitoring and publicly available ground-based measurements. The government said the data provided an empirical basis for assessing the impact of its air pollution control measures and developing targeted interventions. According to the EPCCD, the first reading on Punjab’s real-time air quality portal was published on Oct 1, 2025, with an initial network of 30 regulatory-grade monitoring stations. The network has since expanded to 59 stations, which continuously measure six air pollutants and seven meteorological parameters. The government plans to increase the number of monitoring stations to 100 during the 2025-26 period to strengthen its capacity for monitoring ambient air quality across the province. The department maintained that the expanded network had enabled authorities to make more informed decisions through accurate, ground-based measurements, particularly in contrast to assessments relying on low-cost, non-regulatory sensors and satellite-derived models. The EPCCD also highlighted the role of meteorological conditions in interpreting the improvement. According to official Pakistan Meteorological Department statistics, Lahore received 50pc less rainfall in October 2026 than in October 2025,indicating that the improvement was recorded despite relatively drier conditions. Another important factor in assessing air pollution is the atmospheric boundary layer, also known as the mixing height, which determines the volume of air available to dilute and disperse pollutants. The department said ground-based measurements conducted by the SUPARCO using a ceilometer in Lahore showed an increase of only 10 meters in the minimum mixing layer height during the comparison period. This finding was presented in contrast to a 25-meter increase cited by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI). The EPCCD questioned the reliability of the latter assessment, arguing that ground-based instruments provided more appropriate measurements for evaluating local air quality interventions. The department also referred to peer-reviewed research published in January 2026, which identified systematic biases of between 200 and 500 meters in ERA5 reanalysis data over the monsoon region. It said such model-derived products were useful for regional research but had limitations when used to assess the local impact of air pollution control policies. Alongside monitoring infrastructure, the Punjab government has been implementing a multi-sectoral air pollution reduction strategy targeting transport, industrial emissions, brick kilns and agricultural burning. In the transport sector, the government has introduced 612 electric buses while also providing electric bikes and improving traffic management to reduce emissions from conventional vehicles. The department said around 500,000 vehicles had undergone emissions testing while more than 800 legal notices had been issued to heavy transport vehicles over emissions and fitness certification requirements. The government aims to expand its electric bus fleet to 3,000 vehicles as part of its clean mobility strategy. Industrial compliance has also been strengthened through the Environment Protection Force, which monitors emissions, fuel quality and fugitive dust control systems at more than 600 sites across Punjab. The department said industries emitting excessive smoke without adequate emission-control systems, as well as units using unauthorized fuels, were not allowed to operate. The government has also imposed a complete ban on the operation of tyre pyrolysis plants and the use of carbon powder as industrial fuel, citing concerns over hazardous emissions. Agricultural emissions, particularly those caused by the burning of crop residue, remain another major component of the anti-smog strategy. The EPCCD said field-level stubble-burning incidents had declined by one-third during the first year after the government provided 10,000 super seeders to farmers through targeted subsidies. The government plans to increase the number of subsidized super seeders to 25,000 and introduce additional mechanized solutions,including Kubota harvesters and stubble balers, to discourage open burning and facilitate the use of crop residue as industrial fuel.

Another important factor in assessing air pollution is the atmospheric boundary layer, also known as the mixing height, which determines the volume of air available to dilute and disperse pollutants. The EPCCD questioned the reliability of the latter assessment, arguing that ground-based instruments provided more appropriate measurements for evaluating local air quality interventions. The department also referred to peer-reviewed research published in January 2026, which identified systematic biases of between 200 and 500 meters in ERA5 reanalysis data over the monsoon region. It said such model-derived products were useful for regional research but had limitations when used to assess the local impact of air pollution control policies. Alongside monitoring infrastructure, the Punjab government has been implementing a multi-sectoral air pollution reduction strategy targeting transport, industrial emissions, brick kilns and agricultural burning. In the transport sector, the government has introduced 612 electric buses while also providing electric bikes and improving traffic management to reduce emissions from conventional vehicles. 
The department said around 500,000 vehicles had undergone emissions testing while more than 800 legal notices had been issued to heavy transport vehicles over emissions and fitness certification requirements.
The government aims to expand its electric bus fleet to 3,000 vehicles as part of its clean mobility strategy.
Industrial compliance has also been strengthened through the Environment Protection Force, which monitors emissions, fuel quality and fugitive dust control systems at more than 600 sites across Punjab. 
The department said industries emitting excessive smoke without adequate emission-control systems, as well as units using unauthorized fuels, were not allowed to operate.
The government has also imposed a complete ban on the operation of tyre pyrolysis plants and the use of carbon powder as industrial fuel, citing concerns over hazardous emissions.
Agricultural emissions, particularly those caused by the burning of crop residue, remain another major component of the anti-smog strategy. 
The EPCCD said field-level stubble-burning incidents had declined by one-third during the first year after the government provided 10,000 super seeders to farmers through targeted subsidies.
The government plans to increase the number of subsidized super seeders to 25,000 and introduce additional mechanized solutions,including Kubota harvesters and stubble balers, to discourage open burning and facilitate the use of crop residue as industrial fuel.

headline: US votes in midterm elections seen as referendum on Trump
description: WASHINGTON - Americans struggling with high prices and angry over an unpopular war with Iran began voting on Tuesday in one of the most consequential
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
WASHINGTON - Americans struggling with high prices and angry over an unpopular war with Iran began voting on Tuesday in one of the most consequential elections, widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump’s second term.

Voters in several US states, including New York, Georgia and South Carolina, have been casting their ballots this morning, joining millions who did so before Election Day.

The stakes are high for both parties as Democrats attempt to gain control of both the House and Senate. Democrats entered Election Day with a 9-point advantage in the generic congressional ballot, according to CNN’s Poll of Polls. Meanwhile, Republicans face tests of their redistricting strategy and their grip on Senate seats in solidly red states.

At stake in the elections are all 435 seats of the House and 37 seats in the 100-member Senate.

Elections are also being held for the post of Governor in 36 states. On Monday, the Republicans and the Democrats made their final pitch to the voters, with Trump choosing an unusual venue the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool to focus on the renovations undertaken in the national capital instead of talking about tax cuts, tariffs and border security, which have been the high points of his election rallies.

With more than $1.48 billion wagered on Tuesday’s US midterm elections, prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket are facing their biggest test yet of how reliably they can forecast political races amid growing scrutiny of their businesses.

The platforms rose to prominence in 2024 when they bucked traditional opinion polls in signaling that Donald Trump would win the presidency, and have since amassed a global following among media outlets and investors.

According to the White House, Trump did a whirlwind tour of 20 states, mostly Republican strongholds, to address 30 rallies in the last 32 days. Analysts say his approval ratings are at an all-time low, and he has become a liability to Republican candidates.

If the pre-poll forecasts come true and Democrats take control of the US Congress, it will allow for deeper Congressional scrutiny and checks of Trump’s actions, which will severely limit his ability to push his agenda. He will, however, retain the power to govern through executive orders, which will be valid for two years.

Trump acknowledged the possibility of his wings being clipped but indicated that he will not allow Congress to slow him down.

“I guess I’ll become Mr Veto,” Trump told the New York Postin response to a question on Republicans losing control of both Houses of the US Congress.

Former President Barack Obama boosted the Democratic campaign with rallies in Ohio, Michigan and Georgia, which clearly left Trump rattled.

“This election is our last, best chance of at least reining him in, reining in some of the foolishness of this administration,” Obama said in Georgia.

The Democrats, however, suffered an unexpected setback in the eleventh hour when Congresswoman Haley Stevens of Michigan crossed over to the Republican side on Sunday, breaking ranks with Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who could be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

The Democratic Party quickly rallied behind El-Sayed by issuing statements condemning Stevens, who sprung a surprise by endorsing El-Sayed’s Republican rival, Mike Rogers, and appearing alongside him in public.

Stevens lost in the Senate primary to El-Sayed. She is a staunch supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed is a fierce critic of the US ally.

The Democrats are hoping to flip seven Senate seats: Michigan, Maine, Ohio, Kansas, Texas, Iowa and Alaska in their bid to gain a majority in the 100-member House.

Each of the 50 states in the United States is represented by two Senators who sit in the Congress for a six-year term. But the Senators are divided into three lots, and their terms are staggered so that elections are held every two years.

The mid-term elections are also crucial for Vice President J D Vance, who is burnishing his credentials to become a successor to Trump’s mantle.

Vance made campaign stops in New York and Ohio on Monday, where Republicans were fighting for House and Senate seats.

He highlighted Trump’s moves to end taxes on tips and overtime and secure the border while branding Democrats as “lunatics” who have contempt for American voters.

About 210 million Americans are registered to vote, according to USAFacts. California has the most registered voters, with 23.2 million, followed by Texas (17.4 million) and Florida (13.6 million). Together, they account for about 26 percent of all registered voters.

According to the AP, more than 57 million ballots have been cast in 47 states and D.C. as of Monday, with turnout surpassing the early vote four years ago in many closely watched states.

Meanwhile, The United States has launched “defensive strikes” on Iran’s Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz on the eve of crucial midterm elections, according to US officials.

Iranian state news agency IRNA confirmed several explosions on the island on Monday.

The US officials described the strikes as limited and said they were in response to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing upon a US aircraft.

The strikes appeared to be limited as opposed to a return to full hostilities but followed President Donald Trump previously saying the US wouldn’t launch strikes on Iran before Tuesday’s midterms. The strikes were reported by The Wall Street Journal and CBS News.

The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on US gasoline prices and other parts of the economy have been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress.

The administration was last known to have carried out some attacks in early September, but thousands of US troops remain in the waters off Iran to maintain a naval blockade aimed at preventing tankers carrying Iranian oil from getting to the global market. A third aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are on their way to the Middle East.

Iran’s top security official says the US response to the latest ceasefire offer was “not convincing.”

“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing,” writes Supreme National Security Secretary Mohsen Rezaei on X, “and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them; only then will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”

Among Iran’s demands are a permanent end to the war, including Israel’s operations against Hamas and Hezbollah; the lifting of the US blockade on Iran; the withdrawal of US forces; lifting sanctions; paying reparations for the war; and recognizing new arrangements for shipping in Hormuz that Iran will set.

Earlier Monday, US Vice President JD Vance offered optimism that a deal can still be struck to prevent Trump from following through on his threat to potentially order new strikes on Iran after the midterm elections.

Vance sent a letter to Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, last week, but the White House has offered scant details about the contents. Trump told reporters that the letter was focused on assisting Iran with “medical supplies and various things.”

But Vance on Monday suggested there’s reason to believe that the US and Iran could still come to an agreement.

“We’ve had a number of good conversations with the Iranians,” Vance told reporters on Monday when asked about the letter. “I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this. Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We’re going to keep on working at it.”

Vance’s comments came as the region remains on edge about the prospects of the US resuming full-scale operations against Iran. The backchannel efforts are playing out as Israel and some Middle East allies lobby Trump on the way ahead in the 8-month-old war that has rattled global markets and wreaked havoc on Iran.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday’s elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week’s elections. Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes and pushing for a deal with Iran.

The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran’s ports.

They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American and Israeli officials.

One official said Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the US administration to persuade Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.

Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.

Other US allies in the Middle East are warning against more strikes, saying that would destabilize the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.

Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman said he spoke by phone on Monday with US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth about “the latest regional and international developments” and the Houthis’ continued attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Oil prices dropped sharply on Monday as renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war between the US and Iran appeared to show signs of headway. Rising prices at the pump, a byproduct of the war, have been a weight on Trump’s Republican Party as it tries to maintain control of both chambers of Congress.

Trump noted the drop in a speech in Washington on Monday, which was billed as his closing argument to Americans, and sought to minimize the scale of the conflict, which has cost US taxpayers at least $47 billion.

“I don’t know if you even call it a war, because we haven’t been doing any fighting for months,” Trump said.

Netanyahu has not commented on Iran since the Israeli election, and there was no word from his office on the latest call with Trump.

Iranian officials say publicly they are prepared for war or diplomacy.

Iran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA earlier that “very intensive” talks to try and end the war are under way with the US via mediators.

He also said Tehran was prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios “more than ever before” and that it was up to the US to choose between a “wise path” of negotiation or the “mistake of military aggression”.

But Iran wants guarantees that the US will implement its side of any agreement. The US and Israel have twice attacked Iran while it was engaged in negotiations over its disputed nuclear program.

The new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, met with Iran’s military chiefs and said the response to “any kind and level of threat” from the US or Israel should be immediate and without “geographic limits,” and urged an expansion of the list of potential targets.

A recent analysis by The Associated Press found that Iranian strikes on more than two dozen US bases since the start of the war have caused billions of dollars in equipment damage.

Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, told state television that “the tone has completely changed” from the US and called it a “very good sign.” He also gave no details about the letter he received from Vance, which Iran acknowledged last week, and said he had not responded.

Meanwhile, Vance told reporters on Monday that the Republican administration’s foremost concern is Iran agreeing to take substantive action on its nuclear program.

“We do think that there is a pathway there, but it really does require a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment that they don’t rebuild that nuclear program,” Vance added.

article_html:
WASHINGTON - Americans struggling with high prices and angry over an unpopular war with Iran began voting on Tuesday in one of the most consequential elections, widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump’s second term.

Voters in several US states, including New York, Georgia and South Carolina, have been casting their ballots this morning, joining millions who did so before Election Day.

The stakes are high for both parties as Democrats attempt to gain control of both the House and Senate. Democrats entered Election Day with a 9-point advantage in the generic congressional ballot, according to CNN’s Poll of Polls. Meanwhile, Republicans face tests of their redistricting strategy and their grip on Senate seats in solidly red states.

Top officials blame others over allegations of illegal transfer of 36 acres land in Muzaffargarh

At stake in the elections are all 435 seats of the House and 37 seats in the 100-member Senate.

Elections are also being held for the post of Governor in 36 states. On Monday, the Republicans and the Democrats made their final pitch to the voters, with Trump choosing an unusual venue the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool  to focus on the renovations undertaken in the national capital instead of talking about tax cuts, tariffs and border security, which have been the high points of his election rallies.

With more than $1.48 billion wagered on Tuesday’s US midterm elections, prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket are facing their biggest test yet of how reliably they can forecast political races amid growing scrutiny of their businesses.

Government plans to turn One Constitution Avenue building into five-star hotel, says Naqvi

The platforms rose to prominence in 2024 when they bucked traditional opinion polls in signaling that Donald Trump would win the presidency, and have since amassed a global following among media outlets and investors.

According to the White House, Trump did a whirlwind tour of 20 states, mostly Republican strongholds, to address 30 rallies in the last 32 days. Analysts say his approval ratings are at an all-time low, and he has become a liability to Republican candidates.

If the pre-poll forecasts come true and Democrats take control of the US Congress, it will allow for deeper Congressional scrutiny and checks of Trump’s actions, which will severely limit his ability to push his agenda. He will, however, retain the power to govern through executive orders, which will be valid for two years.

Punjab CM inaugurates retired soldier’s home under Apni Chhat Apna Ghar scheme

Trump acknowledged the possibility of his wings being clipped but indicated that he will not allow Congress to slow him down.

“I guess I’ll become Mr Veto,” Trump told the New York Postin response to a question on Republicans losing control of both Houses of the US Congress.

Former President Barack Obama boosted the Democratic campaign with rallies in Ohio, Michigan and Georgia, which clearly left Trump rattled.

“This election is our last, best chance of at least reining him in, reining in some of the foolishness of this administration,” Obama said in Georgia.

Ishaq Dar, Iranian envoy discuss bilateral ties and regional developments

The Democrats, however, suffered an unexpected setback in the eleventh hour when Congresswoman Haley Stevens of Michigan crossed over to the Republican side on Sunday, breaking ranks with Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who could be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

The Democratic Party quickly rallied behind El-Sayed by issuing statements condemning Stevens, who sprung a surprise by endorsing El-Sayed’s Republican rival, Mike Rogers, and appearing alongside him in public.

Stevens lost in the Senate primary to El-Sayed. She is a staunch supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed is a fierce critic of the US ally.

Pakistan, Turkmenistan seek stronger academic ties through new education initiatives

The Democrats are hoping to flip seven Senate seats: Michigan, Maine, Ohio, Kansas, Texas, Iowa and Alaska in their bid to gain a majority in the 100-member House.

Each of the 50 states in the United States is represented by two Senators who sit in the Congress for a six-year term. But the Senators are divided into three lots, and their terms are staggered so that elections are held every two years.

The mid-term elections are also crucial for Vice President J D Vance, who is burnishing his credentials to become a successor to Trump’s mantle.

Vance made campaign stops in New York and Ohio on Monday, where Republicans were fighting for House and Senate seats.

He highlighted Trump’s moves to end taxes on tips and overtime and secure the border while branding Democrats as “lunatics” who have contempt for American voters.

About 210 million Americans are registered to vote, according to USAFacts. California has the most registered voters, with 23.2 million, followed by Texas (17.4 million) and Florida (13.6 million). Together, they account for about 26 percent of all registered voters.

According to the AP, more than 57 million ballots have been cast in 47 states and D.C. as of Monday, with turnout surpassing the early vote four years ago in many closely watched states.

Meanwhile, The United States has launched “defensive strikes” on Iran’s Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz on the eve of crucial midterm elections, according to US officials.

Iranian state news agency IRNA confirmed several explosions on the island on Monday.

The US officials described the strikes as limited and said they were in response to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing upon a US aircraft.

The strikes appeared to be limited as opposed to a return to full hostilities but followed President Donald Trump previously saying the US wouldn’t launch strikes on Iran before Tuesday’s midterms. The strikes were reported by The Wall Street Journal and CBS News.

The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on US gasoline prices and other parts of the economy have been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress.

The administration was last known to have carried out some attacks in early September, but thousands of US troops remain in the waters off Iran to maintain a naval blockade aimed at preventing tankers carrying Iranian oil from getting to the global market. A third aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are on their way to the Middle East.

Iran’s top security official says the US response to the latest ceasefire offer was “not convincing.”

“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing,” writes Supreme National Security Secretary Mohsen Rezaei on X, “and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them; only then will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”

Among Iran’s demands are a permanent end to the war, including Israel’s operations against Hamas and Hezbollah; the lifting of the US blockade on Iran; the withdrawal of US forces; lifting sanctions; paying reparations for the war; and recognizing new arrangements for shipping in Hormuz that Iran will set.

Earlier Monday, US Vice President JD Vance offered optimism that a deal can still be struck to prevent Trump from following through on his threat to potentially order new strikes on Iran after the midterm elections.

Vance sent a letter to Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, last week, but the White House has offered scant details about the contents. Trump told reporters that the letter was focused on assisting Iran with “medical supplies and various things.”

But Vance on Monday suggested there’s reason to believe that the US and Iran could still come to an agreement.

“We’ve had a number of good conversations with the Iranians,” Vance told reporters on Monday when asked about the letter. “I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this. Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We’re going to keep on working at it.”

Vance’s comments came as the region remains on edge about the prospects of the US resuming full-scale operations against Iran. The backchannel efforts are playing out as Israel and some Middle East allies lobby Trump on the way ahead in the 8-month-old war that has rattled global markets and wreaked havoc on Iran.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday’s elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week’s elections. Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes and pushing for a deal with Iran.

The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran’s ports.

They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American and Israeli officials.

One official said Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the US administration to persuade Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.

Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.

Other US allies in the Middle East are warning against more strikes, saying that would destabilize the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.

Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman said he spoke by phone on Monday with US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth about “the latest regional and international developments” and the Houthis’ continued attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Oil prices dropped sharply on Monday as renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war between the US and Iran appeared to show signs of headway. Rising prices at the pump, a byproduct of the war, have been a weight on Trump’s Republican Party as it tries to maintain control of both chambers of Congress.

Trump noted the drop in a speech in Washington on Monday, which was billed as his closing argument to Americans, and sought to minimize the scale of the conflict, which has cost US taxpayers at least $47 billion.

“I don’t know if you even call it a war, because we haven’t been doing any fighting for months,” Trump said.

Netanyahu has not commented on Iran since the Israeli election, and there was no word from his office on the latest call with Trump.

Iranian officials say publicly they are prepared for war or diplomacy.

Iran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA earlier that “very intensive” talks to try and end the war are under way with the US via mediators.

He also said Tehran was prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios “more than ever before” and that it was up to the US to choose between a “wise path” of negotiation or the “mistake of military aggression”.

But Iran wants guarantees that the US will implement its side of any agreement. The US and Israel have twice attacked Iran while it was engaged in negotiations over its disputed nuclear program.

The new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, met with Iran’s military chiefs and said the response to “any kind and level of threat” from the US or Israel should be immediate and without “geographic limits,” and urged an expansion of the list of potential targets.

A recent analysis by The Associated Press found that Iranian strikes on more than two dozen US bases since the start of the war have caused billions of dollars in equipment damage.

Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, told state television that “the tone has completely changed” from the US and called it a “very good sign.” He also gave no details about the letter he received from Vance, which Iran acknowledged last week, and said he had not responded.

Meanwhile, Vance told reporters on Monday that the Republican administration’s foremost concern is Iran agreeing to take substantive action on its nuclear program.

“We do think that there is a pathway there, but it really does require a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment that they don’t rebuild that nuclear program,” Vance added.

headline: Govt assures domestic consumers of meeting gas demand in winter

author: Fawad Yousafzai
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Amid a supply disruption caused by the closure of the Iranian border, which has pushed LPG prices to Rs700/kg, the federal government has taken swift action to end the monopoly of a few private companies by directing four state-owned companies to start importing LPG and holding transparent auctions.

Addressing a press conference in alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Federal Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said that Pakistan State Oil (PSO), Sui Southern Gas Company, Pakistan LNG Limited and PARCO had been directed to import LPG, while local supplies would be auctioned transparently in five-tonne and 10-tonne lots.

The petroleum minister said Pakistan consumed around 2.4 million tonnes of LPG annually, with more than half met through imports. The closure of Iranian border crossings had created shortages, allowing some market players to sell LPG at Rs700-800 per kilogram, well above the international-market-based price of around Rs450.

Malik said the government will make every effort to maintain gas supply through the pipeline network during breakfast, lunch and dinner hours during the winter season. He said if necessary, additional LNG will also be imported to meet domestic requirements, while rationing can be considered if ircumstances demand. He said Pakistan’s annual LPG demand stands at approximately 2.4 million tonnes, while domestic production is around 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes per day. The remaining requirement is met through imports, including supplies previously received through the western border and sea routes.

The Minister for Petroleum said disruptions in supplies through the western border have created additional challenges, highlighting the need to diversify import sources and strengthen the country’s energy infrastructure.

He said the Prime Minister has directed the formulation of a comprehensive energy security framework, including improvements in storage facilities, refineries and LPG import infrastructure.

Ali Pervaiz Malik said the government has decided to introduce competition in the LPG sector to ensure the availability of the commodity at the lowest possible cost to consumers.

He said state-owned companies, including Pakistan State Oil, Sui gas companies and Pakistan LNG Limited, have been directed to arrange bulk LPG purchases through government-to-government and business-to-business agreements. The private sector will also be encouraged to import LPG, which will increase supply and promote competition.

The minister said all importing companies will publish details of their monthly procurement costs, including Saudi Aramco’s contract price, premiums and freight charges, on their websites to ensure transparency.

He further said the existing quota-based system for locally produced LPG will also be replaced with a transparent auction mechanism. Companies will offer the commodity in lots of five to ten tonnes, and auction results will be made public under the supervision of the relevant authorities.

Ali Pervaiz Malik said the government has also taken measures to protect low-income households from the impact of international price fluctuations. Under the LPG policy, ten percent of the quota reserved for hard areas will be distributed transparently through state-owned companies in consultation with provincial authorities.

He said additional revenue generated through the new pricing and auction mechanism will be channelled into a Price Stabilisation Fund and a Vulnerable Protection Fund to provide subsidized LPG to deserving consumers.

The minister said the Competition Commission has also been directed to prevent market manipulation and the formation of cartels, while OGRA will further improve transparency in its licensing and regulatory procedures.

The relevant authorities will also monitor the quality and safety of LPG cylinders and transportation vehicles through a track-and-trace mechanism.

Ali Pervaiz Malik estimated that the international market price of imported LPG, after including premiums and other costs, can range between 450 and 500 rupees per kilogram.

He said the government will provide targeted relief to deserving consumers through the differential fund mechanism, with subsidized rates to be determined by the Prime Minister.

Speaking on the occasion, Attaullah Tarar said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has placed the protection of public interests at the forefront during the ongoing crisis. He said the government did not allow any additional burden to fall on the people.

The minister said the government has also decided to promote competition in the liquefied petroleum gas sector to facilitate consumers.

He said the government transferred profits earned by refineries to the public, adding that such an initiative has never been undertaken in the country’s history. Attaullah Tarar said all measures taken by the Prime Minister are aimed at providing relief to the people.

headline: 2 policemen guarding polio workers shot dead in KP’s Mohmand
description: PESHAWAR - Gunmen riding a motorcycle shot and killed two police officers assigned to protect polio workers during a door-to-door vaccination campaign Tuesday
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
PESHAWAR - Gunmen riding a motorcycle shot and killed two police officers assigned to protect polio workers during a door-to-door vaccination campaign Tuesday in Mohmand district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, officials said.

The drive-by shooting in Mohmand district that borders Afghanistan also wounded a third police official.

The policemen were traveling to a nearby village to guard vaccination teams when they came under fire, police officer Ayaz Khan told reporters.

The attackers fled the scene. No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack.

The Pakistani Taliban regularly target anti-polio drives and police protecting health workers, falsely claiming that polio vaccination campaigns are part of a Western conspiracy to sterilize children.

In Islamabad, Pakistan’s Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the attack was “intolerable” and offered his condolences to the families of the killed officers, who he said worked for a healthier future for the country.

Separately, suspected militants the previous day abducted four polio workers in Tank, another district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, according to a statement from provincial Gov. Faisal Karim Kundi. He condemned the abductions and urged authorities to take immediate steps to secure the workers’ safe release as soon as possible.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif strongly condemned the firing on police personnel deployed to protect an anti-polio team in Mohmand district. The prime minister paid tribute to those martyred in the incident, prayed for the elevation of their ranks and expressed his condolences to the bereaved families, a Prime Minister’s Office news release said. He said anti-polio workers, along with the police and security personnel assigned to protect them, were performing a national duty and playing their part in securing a safe future for the nation. “Such terrorist attacks are deeply regrettable and worthy of condemnation,” the prime minister said. He reaffirmed the government’s resolve to eradicate terrorism from the country in all its forms.

Pakistan began a nationwide campaign Monday to vaccinate 24 million children against polio as part of efforts to eradicate the disease. Pakistan and neighboring Afghanistan remain the only countries where wild poliovirus is endemic, according to the World Health Organization.

The attacks highlight persistent security threats to Pakistan’s efforts to eradicate the crippling disease, which remains endemic only in Pakistan and neighboring Afghanistan. The latest campaign aims to vaccinate nearly 24 million children under five across 97 districts from Nov. 2 to 8.

The latest incidents came two days after Pakistan confirmed its eighth polio case of 2026, involving a 13-month-old girl in Khyber district, according to the National Emergency Operations Center for Polio Eradication. Six of this year’s eight cases have been reported in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with the remaining two in Sindh province.

Although infections have declined sharply from previous years, the virus continues to circulate in high-risk areas, posing a threat to children who miss vaccination.

Pakistan reported 31 polio cases in 2025, down from 74 in 2024, according to government figures.

The National Emergency Operations Center said more than 6.68 million children received polio drops on Monday, the first day of the latest campaign, which involves over 200,000 health workers going door to door. More than 1.37 million children were vaccinated in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa alone on the opening day, it added.

headline: Three-day 10th Pakistan Industrial Expo to begin on 14th
description: LAHORE - The 10th Pakistan Industrial Expo (PIE 2026) will be held from November 14 to 16 at Expo Centre Lahore, bringing together Pakistani and Chinese
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: LAHORE - The 10th Pakistan Industrial Expo (PIE 2026) will be held from November 14 to 16 at Expo Centre Lahore, bringing together Pakistani and Chinese manufacturers, investors and technology providers to promote industrial cooperation, technology transfer and investment opportunities. The details of the three-day exhibition were shared at a press conference, where organisers and industry representatives highlighted its focus on emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, industrial automation, CNC machinery and smart manufacturing. Fa Wenyan, CEO of Everest International Expo (China), said the Pakistan Industrial Expo had served as a bridge between Pakistani industries and Chinese manufacturing expertise since 2017. He said the 10th edition would further strengthen cooperation in technology transfer, local manufacturing, investment and employment generation.

headline: Pakistan successfully tests first indigenously developed air-to-air missile Fa’az
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan on Tuesday conducted successful flight test of first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile. According to a press release
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan on Tuesday conducted successful flight test of first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile. According to a press release issued by the Inter-Services Public Relation (ISPR), it marks another significant milestone in the advancement of national aerospace and defense capabilities.

The missile is equipped with state of the art terminal guidance system, it can engage enemy aerial targets at longer ranges. Fa’az will significantly enhance operational flexibility of Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country’s overall defense posture.

The successful flight test underscores the technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance achieved by Pakistan’s defense industry.

The launch was witnessed by senior officers of the Pakistan Armed Forces, along with distinguished scientists and engineers who played a pivotal role in the development of this advanced weapon system.

The President, the Prime Minister of Pakistan, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defense Forces and Services Chiefs congratulated the scientists and engineers on this remarkable achievement.

headline: UK, Pakistani bank launch fully funded Chevening scholarships for Pak students
description: ISLAMABAD - The United Kingdom and Allied Bank Limited (ABL) yesterday launched a landmark scholarship partnership to enable talented Pakistanis to pursue
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The United Kingdom and Allied Bank Limited (ABL) yesterday launched a landmark scholarship partnership to enable talented Pakistanis to pursue fully funded master’s degrees at leading British universities, opening new opportunities for higher education and professional development. Under the Chevening-ABL Scholarship programme, two Pakistani scholars will receive financial support annually over three academic years, beginning in 2027-28, to study disciplines critical to Pakistan’s future development, including artificial intelligence, technology, cybersecurity, digital transformation, economics and financial inclusion. Allied Bank has become the first organisation in Pakistan to establish a locally funded Chevening Scholarship partnership, bringing together the UK Government’s flagship international scholarship programme and Pakistan’s private sector to invest in emerging national leadership. British High Commissioner Jane Marriott said Pakistan’s greatest strength was its people and expressed confidence that the partnership would enable promising future leaders to study at world-leading British universities and bring innovative ideas and expertise back home. “It is especially fitting that a former Chevening Scholar is now opening the same door for the next generation,” she said. The first two Chevening-ABL scholars will be selected from the existing applicant pool for the 2027-28 academic year. Applications for the 2028-29 Chevening-ABL Scholarships are expected to open in August 2027 alongside the regular Chevening application cycle, with successful candidates commencing their studies in the United Kingdom in 2028.

headline: CM Maryam sends Rs 5b defamation notice to federal minister Salik over corruption allegations
description: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has served a legal notice on Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has served a legal notice on Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Chaudhry Salik Hussain, demanding withdrawal of his allegations of widespread corruption in Punjab and payment of Rs5 billion in damages for what she described as defamatory remarks.

The legal notice, issued through Additional Advocate General Punjab Ch Muhammad Nawaz, has also been served on ARY News anchor Naeem Ashraf Butt, who interviewed the federal minister, and ARY Chairman Muhammad Iqbal for facilitating and broadcasting the allegedly defamatory statements.

The notice relates to an interview with Chaudhry Salik Hussain broadcast on ARY News on November 2, 2026, in which the federal minister made remarks about alleged corruption in Punjab. During the interview, he reportedly said: “I do not have evidence, but I hear stories about corruption in Punjab every day,” adding that “cupboards, not files, are filled with corruption cases in Punjab.”

According to the legal notice, the minister made sweeping allegations about corruption in the provincial administration despite admitting that he possessed no evidence to substantiate them.

It maintains that the remarks created an impression among viewers that corruption was widespread across the provincial administration, without identifying any particular department, public office, official, project, transaction or inquiry to support the claims.

The notice argues that a federal minister is expected to exercise responsibility while making allegations against another constitutional government and cannot convert hearsay into apparent facts or make sweeping accusations without credible evidence. It also holds the ARY News anchor responsible for introducing and pursuing the subject without seeking clarification or demanding documentary evidence from the interviewee. The notice says responsible journalism required the host to establish the factual basis of such serious allegations before broadcasting them.

The ARY chairman has also been made a recipient of the notice for facilitating and broadcasting the interview. Describing the remarks as false, baseless and defamatory, the chief minister maintains that they have undermined public confidence in the integrity of the Punjab government and her leadership.

The notice acknowledges the importance of freedom of expression, responsible journalism and the right of public representatives to question government performance. However, it argues that these rights do not provide an unrestricted licence to circulate unverified allegations or damage the reputation of others through unsupported assertions.

Maryam Nawaz has given the three recipients seven days to withdraw and unequivocally retract the allegations, publish an unconditional apology and clarification on the same media platforms with prominence equivalent to the original broadcast, and remove or correct the allegedly defamatory portions of the interview and related clips.

She has also demanded Rs5 billion in damages for the alleged harm to her reputation. The notice further directs the recipients to preserve the complete original interview, unedited footage, audio recordings, editorial notes, publication records, relevant communications and available broadcast analytics for possible use in legal proceedings.

It warns that failure to comply with the demands within seven days will compel the chief minister to initiate legal proceedings, including under the Punjab Defamation Act, 2024, before the competent forum. The notice stated that it has been issued without prejudice to any other legal remedies available to the chief minister under the Constitution and laws of Pakistan.

Earlier, addressing a laptop and Honhaar Scholarship distribution ceremony at COMSATS University, Attock, Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Tuesday announced that she was sending a defamation notice to Federal Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain over his allegations of corruption against the Punjab government, challenging him to produce evidence to substantiate his claims.

The chief minister stated the federal minister from Gujrat had alleged that cupboards in Punjab were filled with money earned through corruption. She termed the allegations baseless and said she would serve a legal action on him.

“Trillions of rupees are being invested in development projects in Punjab, with individual projects worth Rs300 billion each. I can take an oath before these children that I have not committed corruption of even a single rupee,” she said.

Maryam Nawaz said she was answerable to the people and Allah Almighty if any wrongdoing was established, challenging those making allegations to provide evidence instead of spreading accusations.

“If you have evidence, bring it forth — otherwise I will drag you to court,” she warned, questioning why the federal minister continued to serve in a government that he himself considered corrupt.

The chief minister alleged that Salik’s criticism had little to do with corruption or development, claiming that he was unhappy over her decision to replace the deputy commissioner of Gujrat a few days ago. She said the federal minister wanted an officer of his choice appointed to the post.

“I do not appoint deputy commissioners on recommendations because that would amount to a breach of trust. Those appointed through recommendations undermine the country,” she said.

Maryam also took exception to Salik’s remarks describing former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi as the best-ever chief minister of the province. Defending her government’s performance in Gujrat, she criticised the state of drainage and infrastructure in the city during Elahi’s tenure. Recalling a visit to Gujrat around two years ago, she said the city had been badly affected by rainwater accumulation, with even her Land Cruiser becoming submerged.

“The Gujrat that Pervez Elahi handed me — I went there about two years ago and it was raining. Believe me, the water was up to here,” she said, gesturing towards her neck. “My Land Cruiser was completely submerged,” she added.

She said Gujrat had previously looked more like a village than a developed city, but the situation had now improved considerably. “Now, when it rains, rainwater does not accumulate. That work was not done by the Chaudhrys,” she said.

The chief minister said the Punjab government was distributing laptops and scholarships purely on merit, without discrimination on the basis of political affiliation, recommendations or money.

Turning to the students receiving laptops and Honhaar Scholarships, Maryam Nawaz congratulated them and said she had personally travelled to Attock as a mother to celebrate their achievements. She described the scholarship recipients as the cream of Punjab, saying their success was the result of hard work and perseverance.

“Parents feel immense pride when their children succeed. These students are receiving the reward of their hard work and are entitled to it. There is no need for them to express gratitude; they should claim their rightful due with dignity,” she said.

She said she had come to present her government’s performance report rather than point out the shortcomings of others.

Recalling the struggles of scholarship recipients, she cited the example of a girl whose financial difficulties following her mother’s death had been resolved through the Honhaar Scholarship. She also met a student whose father was a labourer and who was delighted to receive the financial assistance.

She said many talented students in the past had been forced to discontinue their education because of financial constraints, but no student would now be deprived of education for lack of funds.

The chief minister announced that an electric bike scheme for students would also be launched in the coming days, with pink bikes for girls and black bikes for boys, to facilitate their daily commute.

She said the law and order situation had been improved to ensure the safety of girls travelling independently on motorcycles. “Every son and daughter in Punjab enjoys a sense of security. Everyone knows that they are safe in Punjab. Punjab is the only province providing laptops, scholarships and electric bikes to students,” she said, adding that the province also honoured its students with a Guard of Honour.

Maryam Nawaz said development appeared to come to a halt as soon as one crossed Punjab’s borders, where colleges, roads and public transport facilities were lacking.

“I am not a mother who merely points out problems; I work day and night to resolve them,” she remarked.

She also expressed satisfaction over educational initiatives in Attock, saying she was delighted to see a Grammar School alongside a Nawaz Sharif School of Eminence upon entering the district.

She said 300 Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence were being established across Punjab, equipped with air-conditioned classrooms, artificial intelligence labs and science laboratories. Describing the initiative as an educational revolution, she claimed that the standard of these institutions was even better than that of grammar schools.

The chief minister said she loved every child of Punjab as much as her own children and shared a special emotional bond with them. She recalled how a student in Mandi Bahauddin had told her that she was crying with happiness because she wanted to meet her.

“This is a relationship of love and affection, a bond of hearts. Those who indulge in unnecessary criticism cannot understand this relationship between me and the children,” she said, adding that she would respond to their affection with even greater love.

She urged students not to lose heart in the face of criticism, saying success required hard work, perseverance and the ability to overcome challenges.

Maryam Nawaz said 850 kilometres of roads had been constructed in Attock alone. She also referred to the introduction of Green Buses, establishment of bus terminals, free medicines in hospitals and free treatment facilities as part of the government’s initiatives.

She said loans had been disbursed for the construction of 250,000 houses across Punjab. Citing the example of a retired subedar who owned a plot but lacked resources to build a house, she said he had been able to construct his home after receiving a loan of Rs1.5 million.

The chief minister said Attock had received little attention in the past and had looked more like a village than a city. However, a new market had now been developed, while billions of rupees had been spent on sewerage and drainage projects to address the city’s longstanding flooding problem.

She also ordered the provision of transport for the University of Engineering and Technology (UET), Taxila. The chief minister urged students to respect their parents and never speak rudely to them, even when angry. She asked them to express gratitude to their parents for their sacrifices and said respecting parents brought blessings and honour.

She also sought a commitment from students to keep their streets, neighbourhoods, buses and cities clean. She said 200,000 workers were engaged in the Suthra Punjab programme, but even two million workers would not be able to maintain cleanliness if people continued throwing garbage in public places.

Calling for public cooperation, she urged citizens to take responsibility for keeping their surroundings clean. The chief minister also asked young people to pledge that they would never take up arms against their country and nation, regardless of what others said.

“I have heard people saying, ‘What is there in Pakistan?’ I say that everything is in Pakistan,” she said, urging students never to allow the national flag to be lowered. She prayed that Allah Almighty would bless Pakistan with progress and prosperity and enable the young generation to fulfil their parents’ dreams.
