This is only the tip of the iceberg. According to the Peace and Justice Network’s National Gender-Based Violence Report 2021–2025, a staggering 237,216 crimes against women and girls were reported to the police over five years. And that counts only those who dared to reach a police station.

The provincial breakdown should shake any conscience. Punjab accounted for 195,787 cases, or 82.5 per cent of the national total. Sindh followed with 25,107, of which 77 per cent, or 19,289, involved kidnappings and abductions. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, home to 16.5 per cent of Pakistan’s population, reported only 10,210 cases, but cultural taboos prevent many incidents from being reported. Of 2,334 domestic violence cases reported in KP, 1,197 ended in murder. By the time the complaint reached the police, the woman was already dead. Balochistan reported 3,108 cases, but geographic isolation, tribal pressures and institutional failure obscure the true scale.

In 2024 alone, according to police data cited by the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan, 4,175 rapes and 733 gang rapes were registered nationwide. Last week in Lahore, five women were raped in different localities within seven days, including a divorced mother of seven who drives a rickshaw to feed her children.
Behind every number is a name. And in recent years, the names have become impossible to ignore.

In Sindh, it was Fatima Fariro, the ten-year-old maid tortured to death in a feudal lord’s haveli in Khairpur. In Karachi, 18-month-old Aizal died after an alleged sexual assault by a teenage relative. In KP, five-year-old Ayat Noor was abducted in Haripur and later found dead in an unused well. In Balochistan, Dr Mahnoor Nasir, a 29-year-old surgery trainee, had acid thrown on her face in her duty room by a hospital lift operator who had harassed her for months.

In Islamabad, Sarah Inam, a 37-year-old economist, was murdered by her husband, while 17-year-old TikToker Sana Yousaf was killed after refusing a marriage proposal. Rizwana, a 12-year-old housemaid from Sargodha, was brutally tortured in the Islamabad home of a civil judge’s family. Most recently, in Rawalpindi, 45-year-old digital media executive Hina Javed was found dead in her bathroom, her hands tied, mouth gagged and a wire around her neck. Her brother told police she had repeatedly reported abuse.

And yet, conviction remains a fantasy. According to a briefing to the Senate Functional Committee on Human Rights in May, rape conviction rates for 2025 stood at 4 per cent in Punjab, 6 per cent in KP, 12 per cent in Balochistan and 22 per cent in Sindh. The national conviction rate for honour killings still hovers at 0.5 per cent.

The status of women in Pakistan needs serious re-examination. While the world has moved forward, with women standing alongside men, we have lagged far behind. Intoxicated by the opium of cultural superiority, we have denied women both the modern rights progressive societies guarantee and the divine rights Islam ensured fourteen hundred years ago.

A deeper study of Islam shows that women have far more rights than we are taught: the rights to inheritance, divorce, honour, education and property. These are not favours granted by men. These are divine rights.

Consider Hina Javed, who delayed marriage to care for her mother with dementia and later delayed divorce to avoid the stigma of being called a divorced woman. Her story mirrors thousands of others in which women choose silence over so-called stigma.

We have normalised naming and shaming women. It has become acceptable. On Pakistan’s streets, men move like idle spectators, believing they have the right to ogle at women. We have given ogling social recognition. Cheap jokes about women are treated as a prerogative of masculinity. What kind of country is this, where a woman cannot run freely in a park? Why does a grown, educated, taxpaying woman need a car, a driver and a chaperone simply to travel from one place to another? These are symptoms of a deeper ailment.

Recently, Maryam Nawaz Sharif tweeted about the fate of a woman expected to suffer in silence. Her words resonated because every Pakistani woman knows that script. Who determines what deserves silence? Why must a woman justify walking out of a relationship? When Allah Himself has given her the choice to enter marriage through nikah and exit through khula, who are we to take that choice away?

Marriage, children and working on relationships matter. But nowhere does it say a woman must compromise until she becomes a slave, or remain silent until death. Yet we live by that cruel proverb that a woman’s funeral should leave her husband’s home, that her janaza should go out only after marriage. How can a society calling itself Islamic allow such an un-Islamic saying to govern its homes?

Pakistan will not progress by keeping women silent. Sahil’s report notes that 60 per cent of gender crimes happen inside the victim’s home, the place supposed to be safest. A nation that teaches its daughters to suffer quietly teaches its sons that silence is consent. It is time our pulpits spoke about Surah An-Nisa. It is time we taught boys that ogling is not masculinity. And it is time we told women that Allah gave them a voice long before society tried to take it away.

Fe’reeha Idrees

The writer is a journalist and anchor. She tweets @Fereeha.

headline: Cost of Inaction
description: Once again, a polio vaccination drive has been met with bloodshed. Two policemen have been martyred in Mohmand, another injured, while four polio workers have
author: The Nation
article_text:
Once again, a polio vaccination drive has been met with bloodshed. Two policemen have been martyred in Mohmand, another injured, while four polio workers have been abducted in Tank. These are not isolated tragedies, but further reminders of a militant menace that continues to bleed Pakistan through a thousand cuts.

Polio teams have become soft targets for militancy, with terrorists exploiting their vulnerability to spread fear, undermine the state’s writ and sabotage a vital national campaign. Those protecting vaccinators are being slaughtered for performing their duty, while those administering life-saving vaccines must contend with the prospect of abduction or death.

This cannot go on any longer.

Pakistan remains one of only two countries where polio is endemic. Eight cases have already been reported this year, six from KP. Decades of vaccination drives, enormous expenditure and international assistance have yet to break the cycle of missed children, persistent infections and recurring violence.

With Governor’s Rule imposed in KP, the responsibility now rests squarely with the Centre. It can no longer hide behind provincial incompetence or political obstruction. The federal government has assumed the authority to act and must now demonstrate the resolve to use it.

Polio eradication is inseparable from the wider war against terrorism. Militant networks must be dismantled, vaccination teams secured and every vulnerable district brought firmly under the state’s control.

Condemnations, funeral wreaths and promises of action are no substitutes for results. The Centre must ensure that policemen are not sent to their deaths and children are not condemned to preventable paralysis. Anything less is an abdication of duty.

headline: The Blame Game
description: Karachi’s political leadership has perfected one art over the decades: blaming one another for the city’s ruin. Mayor Murtaza Wahab now points to
author: The Nation
article_text:
Karachi’s political leadership has perfected one art over the decades: blaming one another for the city’s ruin. Mayor Murtaza Wahab now points to billions in development schemes and accuses opposition-controlled towns of making excuses, while the opposition questions the quality, transparency and execution of the KMC’s projects. Both sides have accusations to make, but neither has much to show for decades of political stewardship.

The PPP cannot escape the lion’s share of responsibility. Having controlled Sindh’s provincial machinery for decades, it has presided over the systematic deterioration of Pakistan’s largest metropolis. Yet the opposition parties, too, have held municipal responsibilities over the years, and their own records hardly inspire confidence. Claims of limited powers and resources cannot indefinitely excuse administrative incompetence.

The truth is that Karachi has been failed by successive administrations, across political parties and tiers of government. Its broken roads, water shortages, crumbling infrastructure and dysfunctional municipal services are the accumulated consequences of this collective failure.

The mayor’s development announcements are welcome, but expenditure is not achievement. The opposition’s demands for audits are equally legitimate, but accountability must extend to its own jurisdictions. Every rupee spent, every contract awarded and every project completed must withstand independent scrutiny.

Beyond this, Karachi desperately needs structural reform, empowered local institutions and freedom from the political patronage that has strangled its development.

The city’s residents have endured enough political theatre. They deserve functioning infrastructure, competent administration and measurable improvements in their lives. Neither side can claim victory in this blame game when the city they collectively govern remains the ultimate loser.

headline: A Systemic Failure
description: When citizens must write to the prime minister to secure basic civic amenities and protection from alleged exploitation, something has gone terribly wrong with
author: The Nation
article_text:
When citizens must write to the prime minister to secure basic civic amenities and protection from alleged exploitation, something has gone terribly wrong with the institutions meant to serve them. The plight of over 2,000 residents of Islamabad’s Roshan Pakistan Housing Scheme is another reminder of the regulatory dysfunction that has plagued Pakistan’s housing sector for decades.

Residents allege financial extortion, intimidation and the denial of basic amenities, despite investing their life savings in the scheme. The developer denies wrongdoing, maintaining that facilities were provided and fresh charges are necessary for rehabilitation. Yet the dispute raises an uncomfortable question: where has the Capital Development Authority been throughout this ordeal?

The scheme’s regulatory approvals were reportedly suspended in 2017, yet nearly a decade later, residents remain embroiled in disputes over development obligations, charges and regulatory authority. Surely, determining these matters is precisely what the CDA and other relevant institutions exist to do. Pakistan’s housing sector has long been a playground for speculative profiteering, questionable developers and regulatory negligence. Ordinary citizens are left to navigate a bureaucratic labyrinth, while those responsible for oversight either fail to act or intervene only after matters reach a breaking point.

Writing desperate letters to the prime minister should not be a recourse in a functioning administrative system. Nor should the country’s chief executive be expected to personally adjudicate disputes that fall squarely within the jurisdiction of established institutions.

The allegations warrant independent investigation and accountability wherever wrongdoing is established. More importantly, the government must overhaul the regulatory machinery that allows such disputes to fester for years.

A state whose citizens must appeal to its highest office for routine enforcement has failed at its most elementary responsibilities.

headline: Samar Bilour seeks 13-year record of recruitments in KP Relief Dept
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Information and Public Relations, Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement, Samar Haroon
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Information and Public Relations, Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement, Samar Haroon Bilour, has sought a comprehensive record of recruitments, budget allocations and development projects undertaken by the Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement Department over the past 13 years.

She issued these directives while chairing an introductory meeting of the department, which was attended by Secretary Relief Yousaf Rahim and representatives of its attached institutions.

During the meeting, the Secretary Relief briefed the Adviser on the department’s administrative structure, rules and regulations, the responsibilities of its attached institutions, overall performance and reform agenda.

Officials of the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) briefed her on disaster preparedness, early warning systems, emergency planning, damage assessment and compensation for disaster-affected people.

Rescue 1122 officials highlighted their emergency response operations, medical assistance, patient transportation, firefighting and specialised rescue services, while Civil Defence officials outlined their activities relating to public safety, volunteer training and fire safety.

Samar Bilour directed the Secretary Relief to submit a complete and verified record of all recruitments made in the department over the past 13 years. She also sought details of budget allocations, fund releases and utilisation, along with a comprehensive record of Annual Development Programme (ADP) and non-ADP schemes, including their approval, expenditure, implementation progress and completion status.

She directed the officials concerned to ensure transparency and maintain properly documented and verifiable records of all recruitment, financial and development-related matters.

Speaking at the meeting, Samar Bilour said that climate change, terrorism and challenges associated with illegally residing foreign nationals had further increased the importance of the Relief Department and its attached institutions.

She stressed the need for advance disaster preparedness, effective emergency planning and coordinated efforts among relevant departments to ensure timely assistance during emergencies.

She said that providing prompt relief to the public, ensuring an effective emergency response and rehabilitating affected families were among the government’s key priorities.

“A transforming, booming and steadfast Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is our vision,” the Adviser said, adding that institutional reforms, transparency and capacity-building measures would be introduced to improve the performance of the Relief Department and its attached institutions.

She emphasised that all relevant institutions must work collectively to ensure efficient service delivery and provide timely assistance to the public.

headline: Dr Aamer sets deadlines for completion of higher education projects
description: Peshawar - A review meeting on the Annual Development Programme (ADP) 2026–27 for the Higher Education Sector was held under the chairmanship
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - A review meeting on the Annual Development Programme (ADP) 2026–27 for the Higher Education Sector was held under the chairmanship of Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Education and Social Welfare, Dr Aamer Abdullah.

The meeting conducted a detailed review of ongoing and new development projects, their financial progress, fund releases and implementation status.

Secretary Higher Education, Archives and Libraries Abidullah Kakakhel, Special Secretary Fazal Hussain and other relevant departmental officials attended the meeting.

During the meeting, Dr Aamer directed the authorities concerned to expedite work on the remaining phases of development projects involving government colleges that were nearing completion or had already been completed, ensuring that these educational institutions became functional at the earliest.

He emphasised that where projects were facing unnecessary delays despite the release of funds, responsibility should be fixed and the outstanding issues resolved promptly.

He further directed that any impediments caused by the Communication and Works Department in completing or handing over projects should be effectively addressed through the relevant forums.

The Adviser for Education set March 15 as the deadline for completing the project aimed at providing essential facilities in government colleges. He also directed that the project for supplying sports equipment, machinery and other necessary items be completed within one month of its approval.

He stressed the need to expedite the development scheme for repairing existing colleges and constructing additional infrastructure.

Dr Aamer also directed the department to resolve the issue of salaries for employees working under the Quality Assurance Programme in the Higher Education Sector on a priority basis. The relevant officials assured him that the outstanding salaries of programme employees would be released by the following Friday.

The Adviser for Education further directed the department to submit weekly performance reports on the implementation of projects included in the 100-Day Plan of “Badalta Khyber Pakhtunkhwa”. He said the department’s performance would be formally reviewed every Friday to ensure regular monitoring and timely implementation of the planned initiatives.

Regarding the project aimed at improving facilities in hostels of public-sector universities, Dr Aamer directed the authorities concerned to obtain proposals and detailed assessments of requirements from universities for upgrading washrooms, dining areas and common rooms.

He emphasised that these three essential facilities should be given priority, while other requirements should also be identified according to the specific needs of individual universities.

On the occasion, Dr Aamer stated that public funds must be utilised for meaningful and public-oriented development projects whose benefits could be directly enjoyed by citizens. He stressed that unnecessary or ineffective projects should be avoided and directed the Higher Education Department to fulfil its responsibilities by ensuring the relevance, timely completion and effective implementation of all development initiatives.

headline: Kundi orders administrative, academic reforms at Edwardes College
description: Peshawar - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi has directed the authorities concerned to implement fast-track administrative and
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi has directed the authorities concerned to implement fast-track administrative and academic reforms at Edwardes College Peshawar, emphasising that restoring the institution’s academic excellence is among the provincial government’s top priorities.

Chairing a meeting on the college’s administrative and academic affairs, the Governor reviewed various matters relating to governance, infrastructure, digital systems, e-learning, academic performance and students’ achievements.

Adviser to the Governor on Education Dr Amir Abdullah, Secretary Higher Education Abidullah Kakakhel, members of the Board of Governors, the college principal and other relevant officials attended the meeting.

The participants were also briefed on the college’s financial management, administrative reforms, accountability measures, extracurricular activities and tax-related issues.

Expressing dissatisfaction with the institution’s current performance and administrative affairs, Governor Kundi directed the authorities to resolve all outstanding issues on a priority basis and undertake administrative and academic improvements on a fast-track basis.

He tasked Adviser to the Governor on Education Dr Amir Abdullah with overseeing comprehensive reforms at Edwardes College and directed the authorities to complete the process of appointing a permanent principal at the earliest. He also ordered the immediate filling of vacant positions in the college’s pending committees.

Expressing deep concern over the abduction of four polio workers in Tank district, Governor Kundi termed the incident extremely unfortunate and unacceptable. He directed the authorities concerned to take immediate and effective measures to ensure the safe recovery of the abducted polio workers.

headline: Senate panel seeks integrated e-attestation system to end delays
description: ISLAMABAD - The Senate Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs on Tuesday directed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA), Higher Education Commission
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Senate Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs on Tuesday directed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA), Higher Education Commission (HEC) and National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) to develop an integrated electronic document attestation system, expressing concern over delays and high charges despite the digitisation of services.

The committee, chaired by Senator Agha Shahzaib Durrani, called for a comprehensive plan to streamline the attestation process, introduce QR-code-based verification of official documents and minimise unnecessary human interaction.

During its meeting, members questioned why citizens continued to face delays in document attestation despite extensive digitisation of government services. They also urged the Foreign Office to review the fees charged for attesting government-issued documents.

The committee was informed that the Foreign Office had digitised general document attestation, which accounts for around 65 per cent of its total workload, through integration with the HEC database. However, the traditional manual facility has also been retained to facilitate the general public.

The remaining 35 per cent of the workload relates to apostille attestation, for which the ministry is planning to integrate its system with NADRA to make the process faster, more secure and efficient.

Taking notice of public difficulties, Chairman Agha Shahzaib Durrani directed HEC, NADRA and the Foreign Office to present a comprehensive plan for an integrated e-attestation mechanism at the next committee meeting. He also called for QR-code-based verification to ensure instant authentication, prevent document misuse and eliminate unnecessary delays.

The ministry was further directed to launch an awareness campaign to inform citizens about the availability of digitised attestation services.

The committee also reviewed Pakistan’s foreign policy priorities, including relations with Afghanistan, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s recent visit to the United Nations and the country’s diplomatic engagements amid evolving regional and international developments.

Members welcomed the newly appointed Foreign Secretary and appreciated his effective representation of Pakistan’s position during his tenure as the country’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations. However, they expressed concern over the absence of the Foreign Minister, stressing that his participation in committee proceedings was important for meaningful parliamentary oversight and informed deliberations on foreign policy matters.

The committee received a briefing on the Prime Minister’s UN visit and his engagements on the sidelines. Members were also informed that the recent visit of the UN Secretary-General to Pakistan reflected the success of the country’s diplomatic outreach.

The chairman directed the Foreign Office to provide a comprehensive briefing at the next meeting on the Prime Minister’s UN engagements in the context of the Iran-US conflict, the Makkah Pact and emerging regional and international developments.

Reviewing Pakistan’s role in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), the committee was informed about preparations for the country’s leadership role in the organisation, which Pakistan has assumed for the first time.

The ministry outlined plans for engagement with member states through various SCO events, including the upcoming summit, with particular focus on artificial intelligence, regional connectivity, youth engagement and bilateral cooperation.

The committee also discussed Pakistan’s forthcoming engagement with the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Foreign Ministers, emphasising the need to utilise the country’s leadership role in regional forums to advance its economic and strategic interests.

The Foreign Office briefed members on efforts to operationalise inter-regional trade quotas and develop effective transit trade and transportation mechanisms through the ECO platform.

Chairman Durrani stressed that Pakistan must translate its diplomatic engagements and leadership positions in the SCO and ECO into tangible economic gains, improved regional connectivity and stronger bilateral relations. He urged the ministry to adopt a proactive approach to maximise the benefits of participation in regional organisations.

The committee also received an in-camera briefing on the current state of Pakistan-Afghanistan relations, including key issues and recent developments.

The meeting was attended by Senators Sherry Rehman, Rubina Qaim Khani, Anusha Rahman Ahmed and Amir Waliuddin Chishti.

headline: Special cleanliness drive launched in Lower Dir to improve sanitation
description: Timergara - The Local Government and Rural Development Department in Lower Dir on Monday launched a special cleanliness campaign on the directives
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Timergara - The Local Government and Rural Development Department in Lower Dir on Monday launched a special cleanliness campaign on the directives of the district administration to improve sanitation in markets, villages and other areas across the district.

The campaign, titled “Clean and Green Lower Dir,” aims to remove accumulated garbage and waste from urban and rural areas, as well as clear debris generated during anti-encroachment operations to ensure a clean and healthy environment. The campaign was formally inaugurated by Assistant Director of the Local Government and Rural Development Department, Lower Dir, Amir Nizam Durrani, at a ceremony held at Family Park Balambat.

An awareness walk was also organised to highlight the importance of cleanliness and public participation in maintaining a healthy environment.

A large number of departmental officials and staff participated in the inaugural ceremony and carried out a special cleanliness drive at the family park, removing garbage and waste from its premises.

Local social figure Akbar Zeb Akhunkhel and other prominent personalities also attended the event.

Addressing the participants, Amir Nizam Durrani highlighted the importance of cleanliness, environmental protection and preserving the beauty of public spaces. He said that collective efforts by government departments and the public were essential to making Lower Dir clean and green, adding that a clean environment was the foundation of a healthy and beautiful society.

Durrani urged citizens to cooperate with the relevant authorities and play their part in keeping markets, villages and public places clean.

headline: Alpurai College Road in Shangla to reopen for traffic within a week
description: Shangla - The reconstruction and rehabilitation of College Road in Alpurai, the district headquarters of Shangla, is progressing at a fast pace,
author: Aftab Hussain
article_text:
Shangla - The reconstruction and rehabilitation of College Road in Alpurai, the district headquarters of Shangla, is progressing at a fast pace, with the important road expected to be completed and reopened to all types of traffic within the next week.

The project is being supervised by renowned Consultant Engineer Syed Mazhar Ali Shah, while construction work is being carried out in accordance with modern engineering principles, prescribed standards and quality specifications.

According to details, College Road Alpurai is among the most important roads in District Shangla, providing access to several major government institutions and private establishments. These include Government College Alpurai, the Passport Office, SP Investigation Office, League House, Mansoor Doctor Hospital, Bait-ul-Mal Office, Habib Medical Hospital and Ayan Medical Hospital.

In addition to these institutions, hundreds of residential houses are situated along both sides of the road. It also serves as a major route for residents of the upper areas, particularly Lari and Biagali, for their daily commute.

During the recent monsoon and rainy season, continuous landslides, mudslides and falling debris severely damaged the road, leaving it in a dilapidated condition. Deep potholes, a broken surface, accumulated mud and blocked drainage channels had made the road almost impassable.

Due to its deteriorating condition, students of Government College, patients travelling to hospitals, government employees, visitors to public offices and local residents were facing serious transportation difficulties. Ambulances, college buses, private vehicles and pedestrians were particularly affected.

Keeping in view the public importance of the road and the difficulties faced by residents, the authorities launched its reconstruction and rehabilitation on an emergency basis.

Residents of Alpurai, Lari, Biagali and adjoining areas have appreciated the professional capabilities, honesty and dedicated services of Consultant Engineer Syed Mazhar Ali Shah. They expressed hope that the project would be completed in accordance with the prescribed quality standards.

Local residents said that College Road was not merely a road but a lifeline for thousands of people, including students, patients, government employees and other residents.

The important road is expected to be completed and reopened to traffic within the next week, providing considerable relief to residents who have been facing transportation difficulties.

The important road is expected to be completed and reopened to traffic within the next week, providing considerable relief to residents who have been facing transportation difficulties.

headline: AWKUM announces modern academic, career development facilities
description: Mardan - An orientation session for newly admitted students was organised by the Career Counseling and Placement Center at Abdul Wali Khan
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Mardan - An orientation session for newly admitted students was organised by the Career Counseling and Placement Center at Abdul Wali Khan University Mardan (AWKUM), with Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Jamil Ahmed attending as the chief guest.

The session was attended by Director Career Development Center Dr Bilal, Prof. Dr Azam, Dr Aamir, Director Admissions Fazal Sattar Durrani, Principal College of Arts, faculty members and students.

Addressing the gathering, Vice-Chancellor Prof. Dr Jamil Ahmed welcomed the newly admitted students to the university and said that respecting one’s country, educational institution and teachers was essential for achieving success.

He urged students to make Abdul Wali Khan University Mardan a distinguished name through their hard work, character and abilities, emphasising that their admission to the university had been secured on merit.

The Vice-Chancellor said that modern seminar rooms and student grooming centres were being established in every department to enhance students’ academic and professional skills. He added that students would be shifted to a state-of-the-art hostel equipped with modern facilities in January.

He further said that the university’s central library remained open until 7 pm, while a virtual gaming centre was also being established for students. He encouraged them to make hard work and dedication their guiding principles and take full advantage of the facilities available at the university.

Director Career Counseling and Placement Center Dr Bilal said that the university had initiated the implementation of a joint academic programme with Canada’s Trent University under a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). The programme covers Computer Science, Environmental Science and Business Education.

Under this arrangement, students will be able to complete four semesters at Abdul Wali Khan University Mardan and the remaining four semesters at Trent University in Canada, providing them with valuable international academic exposure.

He added that various student societies had also been established at the university, enabling students to participate in extracurricular activities according to their interests and abilities.

Dr Bilal said that the Career Development Center would guide students in future planning, understanding job market requirements, preparing for interviews and developing professional skills to help them succeed in their practical careers.

headline: Woman arrested for stealing gold jewellery worth over Rs3.7m from house in Rawalpindi
description: RAWALPINDI - Civil Lines Police have arrested a woman allegedly involved in stealing gold jewellery worth over Rs3.7 million from a house in the absence of the
author: APP
article_text:
RAWALPINDI - Civil Lines Police have arrested a woman allegedly involved in stealing gold jewellery worth over Rs3.7 million from a house in the absence of the owners.

According to a police spokesperson, the accused woman, who had recently been hired as a domestic worker at the house, was found involved in the theft.

Police recovered stolen gold jewellery worth more than Rs3.7 million from her possession. Civil Lines Police used technical and human intelligence sources to trace and arrest the suspect. Raids are being conducted to apprehend her accomplice, who is also allegedly involved in the crime. Acting on the directions of CPO Rawalpindi Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera, SP Potohar Chaudhry Asar Ali handed over the recovered gold jewellery to the complainant.

SP Potohar Chaudhry Asar Ali said all possible measures were being taken to ensure the protection of citizens’ lives and property.

headline: 2 fresh cases tally 86 confirmed dengue cases in Rawalpindi
description: RAWALPINDI - District Health Authority Rawalpindi has released the dengue prevention and control brief as of Monday, November 2. The data shows a
author: APP
article_text:
RAWALPINDI - District Health Authority Rawalpindi has released the dengue prevention and control brief as of Monday, November 2. The data shows a total of 6,433 patients screened across hospitals this year, resulting in 5,905 suspected cases and 86 confirmed cases, with two fresh cases during last 24 hours.

Hospital admissions currently stand at 11 patients, with 4 confirmed cases admitted and zero deaths reported.

Field operations involve 415 outdoor teams and 985 indoor teams monitoring 17,859 hotspots registered with PITB, achieving a 99 percent coverage rate from the previous week.

The report shows punitive measures against standard operating procedure violations include 2,798 FIRs, 686 sealings, 2,331 challans, and fines totaling Rs. 31,56,000.

The highest larva detection was recorded in Dhoke Mangtal Municipal Corporation Rawalpindi, Narar Kahuta, Rawalpindi Cantonment and Dakhali Kahuta.

headline: 10 more BHUs in Islamabad to offer specialist consultations
description: ISLAMABAD - The District Health Office (DHO) Islamabad has said that in collaboration with Sehat Kahani, 10 additional Basic Health Units (BHUs)
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The District Health Office (DHO) Islamabad has said that in collaboration with Sehat Kahani, 10 additional Basic Health Units (BHUs) would provide specialist healthcare consultations to improve access to quality medical services at the primary healthcare level in the federal capital.

The initiative aims to facilitate patients by providing timely medical advice and specialist consultations closer to their communities.

The expansion is expected to reduce travel difficulties for patients, particularly those requiring specialist medical advice, while helping ease the burden on major hospitals.

The project will strengthen primary healthcare services through technology-based solutions and improve access to medical consultations for residents of Islamabad.

The initiative also supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

The DHO said the initiative reflected ongoing efforts to use digital health solutions to make healthcare services more accessible, efficient and inclusive.

headline: DC Murree reviews healthcare and sanitation standards at THQ Hospital
description: MURREE - Deputy Commissioner Murree, Agha Zaheer Abbas Shirazi paid a surprise visit to Tehsil Headquarter (THQ) Hospital Murree on Tuesday to
author: APP
article_text:
MURREE - Deputy Commissioner Murree, Agha Zaheer Abbas Shirazi paid a surprise visit to Tehsil Headquarter (THQ) Hospital Murree on Tuesday to evaluate healthcare service delivery, pharmaceutical stocks, and clinical sanitation.

During the inspection, he conducted a thorough review of various operational units, including the Outpatient Department (OPD), central laboratory, diagnostic facilities, and main pharmacy.

Issuing instructions to Medical Superintendent THQ Hospital Murree Dr. Mian Owais Alam, the deputy commissioner affirmed that uninterrupted access to free essential medicines and medical care must be ensured for all visiting patients.

He warned that negligence in clinical management, staff presence, or hygiene standards would invite immediate disciplinary action.

He further directed the hospital management to enforce rigorous daily sanitation protocols and optimize operational efficiency across all clinical departments.

headline: Pakistan moves to enforce 2D barcodes on medicines after Oct 9 deadline
description: ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for National Health Services Mustafa Kamal chaired a meeting to review progress on implementing 2D barcodes on
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for National Health Services Mustafa Kamal chaired a meeting to review progress on implementing 2D barcodes on medicines after the October 9 deadline.

The meeting, attended by DRAP CEO, relevant officials and industry stakeholders, was informed that around 80% of pharmaceutical companies had started implementing the 2D barcode system.

The Ministry of Health has decided to issue formal notices to companies that have failed to submit the required data. Companies that do not comply within the stipulated timeframe will face strict legal action, including the sealing of their production units.

Mustafa Kamal stressed that eliminating counterfeit medicines was imperative, declaring a zero-tolerance policy on non-compliance. He directed all pharmaceutical companies to submit their serialization data to DRAP to ensure effective monitoring, transparency, and a robust drug track-and-trace system.

headline: Double standards alleged in Shangla anti-encroachment drive
description: Shangla - Serious allegations of double standards, discrimination and selective enforcement of the law have emerged during the ongoing
author: Aftab Hussain
article_text:
Shangla - Serious allegations of double standards, discrimination and selective enforcement of the law have emerged during the ongoing anti-encroachment operation in District Shangla. Citizens have accused the district administration of demolishing a market on one side of the central Alpurai Bridge while allegedly providing protection to another market belonging to an influential individual on the opposite side of the same bridge.

According to details, several large markets, shops, hotels, roadside cabins and other encroachments have been demolished during the ongoing anti-encroachment drive in different parts of Shangla, including Lilownai, Alpurai, Puran, Chakesar, Besham and other tehsils. The operation, aimed at clearing roads, bazaars, bridges and public passageways of encroachments, is being carried out by the district administration with the assistance of the Tehsil Municipal Administration (TMA), police and other relevant departments.

However, strong public reaction has emerged over what citizens describe as discriminatory action in Alpurai, the district headquarters. Local residents allege that two markets are situated on opposite sides of the main central bridge, which serves as a vital link for the district headquarters.

According to public complaints, the administration conducted a full-scale operation and demolished shops in front of one market, while on the opposite side of the same bridge, only a small pillar belonging to another market, allegedly owned by an influential individual, was removed, leaving the rest of the structure intact.

Citizens have raised serious questions about the manner in which the operation was conducted, describing it as a glaring example of double standards. They have questioned why markets situated on opposite sides of the same bridge are being subjected to different treatment if the anti-encroachment campaign is genuinely being carried out in accordance with the law and without discrimination.

Residents of Alpurai, Puran, Besham, Chakesar, Martung and other areas have clarified that they are not opposed to the anti-encroachment campaign. Rather, they fully support it, maintaining that removing illegal encroachments from roads, bridges, bazaars and public thoroughfares is both an administrative responsibility and a public necessity. Clear roads ensure the smooth flow of traffic, pedestrian safety and the improvement of public spaces. However, they stressed that such action must be taken equally, transparently and impartially against all violators, without favouritism or discrimination.

Residents have particularly questioned the treatment of the market situated on the opposite side of Alpurai’s main bridge.

They alleged that the removal of only a small pillar amounted to a symbolic action intended to create an impression that the operation had been carried out, while the remaining structure was left untouched. In contrast, shops in front of the market on the other side of the bridge were completely demolished. This disparity, they said, has created the impression that personal influence and connections are being given priority over the uniform application of the law.

Public representatives and local residents have alleged that the owner of the market near the bridge is receiving preferential treatment because of political affiliations, personal influence and recommendations, while the shops and businesses of other traders, including poor shopkeepers and roadside cabin owners, are being demolished.

Citizens have called for a transparent, high-level inquiry to establish the facts and determine whether any administrative officials have misused their authority to benefit a particular individual. They demanded that anyone found responsible should face legal action.

Local residents have demanded that the Commissioner Malakand Division and other relevant high authorities immediately order an impartial survey of markets and other structures situated on both sides of the central Alpurai Bridge. They called for encroachments to be identified on the basis of official revenue records and relevant laws, followed by indiscriminate legal action wherever illegal constructions are found.

In particular, citizens have appealed to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi to take immediate notice of the matter and order a high-level inquiry to determine why different standards of enforcement were allegedly adopted on opposite sides of the same bridge in Alpurai.

Residents have reiterated that they stand with the administration in its efforts to eliminate illegal encroachments and support every lawful step taken in this regard.

headline: Pak, Sri Lanka explore cooperation in Buddhist heritage, religious tourism
description: ISLAMABAD - A 20-member Sri Lankan delegation comprising academics, Buddhist monks, religious leaders and media representatives visited the
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - A 20-member Sri Lankan delegation comprising academics, Buddhist monks, religious leaders and media representatives visited the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday to explore avenues for strengthening cultural, religious and academic cooperation between Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

The delegation was briefed by Foreign Office spokesperson Ambassador Sajjad Haider Khan and Director General Strategic Communications Tariq Wazeer on Pakistan’s rich cultural and religious heritage, with particular emphasis on its Gandhara Buddhist legacy, religious tourism potential and initiatives such as the Kartarpur Corridor.

Ambassador Sajjad Haider Khan highlighted the longstanding friendship between Pakistan and Sri Lanka and warmly welcomed Sri Lankan visitors, underscoring Pakistan’s commitment to promoting religious tourism and facilitating greater people-to-people exchanges.

The discussions focused on expanding bilateral cooperation through academic partnerships, improved connectivity, updating existing memorandums of understanding (MoUs), joint archaeological explorations and cultural exchanges.

Ambassador Khan also acknowledged the contributions of Prime Minister’s Taskforce Gandhara Cradle of Buddhism Strategy, Mr. Imran Shaukat, and Sri Lankan High Commissioner to Pakistan, both of whom attended the meeting.

headline: KMU VC participates in WHO meeting on cardiovascular disease in Geneva
description: Peshawar - Professor Dr Abdul Jalil Khan, Vice-Chancellor of Khyber Medical University (KMU), Peshawar, participated in a five-day, in-person
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Professor Dr Abdul Jalil Khan, Vice-Chancellor of Khyber Medical University (KMU), Peshawar, participated in a five-day, in-person meeting of the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Guideline Development Group (GDG) in Geneva, Switzerland, to contribute to the development of international guidelines on the management of dyslipidaemia for the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular diseases.

Prof Jalil Khan, who was previously selected as an expert member of this prestigious WHO committee through an international selection process, is the only expert from Pakistan appointed to the Guideline Development Group. His selection reflects international recognition of his expertise in family medicine, primary healthcare, public health and health systems strengthening.

The WHO Guideline Development Group brings together distinguished international experts from leading academic, clinical and research institutions worldwide. Its members represent a wide range of specialisations, including cardiology, internal medicine, endocrinology, epidemiology, public health and evidence-based guideline development.

The Geneva meeting provided an important opportunity for experts to collectively review scientific evidence and contribute to the development of evidence-based recommendations for the prevention and management of cardiovascular diseases. Particular emphasis was placed on improving the identification and management of dyslipidaemia, a major risk factor for heart attacks and strokes.

Prof Jalil Khan’s participation brought valuable perspectives from primary healthcare systems and low- and middle-income countries, particularly highlighting the importance of developing practical, equitable and evidence-based recommendations that can be implemented across diverse healthcare settings.

With extensive clinical and academic experience in the United Kingdom’s National Health Service (NHS), along with his leadership in family medicine, primary healthcare development and health systems strengthening in Pakistan, Prof Jalil Khan brings a unique combination of international clinical expertise and practical health systems experience to this global initiative.

The development of these WHO guidelines is expected to help countries strengthen cardiovascular disease prevention, improve clinical decision-making and integrate effective non-communicable disease management into primary healthcare services.

Prof Jalil Khan’s participation in this important international initiative highlights the growing contribution of Pakistani healthcare professionals to global health policy and evidence-based guideline development. It also further strengthens Khyber Medical University’s international academic standing and its role in global health initiatives.

headline: KP adviser directs special legal audit of cases involving financial implications
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Law, Labour and Inter-Provincial Coordination, Amir Javed, has directed the authorities
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Law, Labour and Inter-Provincial Coordination, Amir Javed, has directed the authorities to conduct a special legal audit of cases involving significant financial implications. He issued these directives while chairing a meeting convened to review the individual performance of District Attorneys posted in various districts of the province.

Taking notice of the failure of some District Attorneys to provide the required details regarding the financial implications of cases during the meeting, he directed that warning notices be issued to them. Amir Javed made it clear that all District Attorneys were bound to provide complete financial details of the cases concerned and that any negligence or lack of cooperation in this regard would not be tolerated.

He further directed that the performance of each District Attorney be reviewed individually, with a detailed assessment of case follow-ups, court decisions and their financial implications.

He emphasised that the exercise was essential to safeguarding the financial interests of government institutions, ensuring effective monitoring of legal affairs and strengthening institutional accountability.

headline: DC pledges joint efforts for sustainable uplift in Tank
description: Tank - Deputy Commissioner Tank Jamshed Khan and members of the Advisory Council have reaffirmed their commitment to promoting sustainable
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Tank - Deputy Commissioner Tank Jamshed Khan and members of the Advisory Council have reaffirmed their commitment to promoting sustainable development, ensuring lasting peace and addressing public issues through coordinated efforts.

The commitment was expressed during a meeting between Deputy Commissioner Jamshed Khan and Advisory Council members Abdullah Nangyal, Irfanullah Kundi and Nawabzada Wahab Khan.

During the meeting, participants held detailed discussions on the challenges facing the district, public concerns and ongoing and proposed development projects. They also emphasised the importance of effective coordination among all relevant departments to ensure the timely completion of development schemes, improve public service delivery and create greater economic opportunities for local residents.

Speaking on the occasion, the Deputy Commissioner said that their shared objective was to transform Tank into a peaceful, self-reliant and prosperous district by strengthening local resources, promoting sustainable development and empowering the community through collective efforts.

He expressed confidence that close coordination among all stakeholders would accelerate the pace of development and improve the quality of life of the people of the district.

article_text:
The US has no immediate plans to strike Iran, President Donald Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday.

In an interview with the newspaper hours before polls closed in US midterm elections, Trump described Washington's position toward Iran as a “brilliant situation,” suggesting the administration was satisfied with the current balance of pressure on Tehran.

“We seem to be getting everything we want,” he said.

Asked about indications from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that an attack could take place later this week, Trump said American forces remained prepared to act but suggested that military action might not be necessary.

“I’m ready, we’re ready. We’re locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it,” he said.

Trump argued that the US was not currently engaged in a conventional war with Iran, pointing to previous American military operations against the country's nuclear infrastructure.

“We’re not really in a war, because we hit them with the B-2 bombers and wiped out their nuclear potential incapacity,” he said, referring to the earlier US bombing campaign.

He also referenced Operation Epic Fury and subsequent military actions, arguing that the confrontation did not resemble major conventional conflicts such as World War I, World War II or the ongoing war in Ukraine.

“I don’t consider that we’re in a war like Ukraine, wars like World War I, World War II,” he said.

Despite his assessment, the president acknowledged that Washington remained concerned about Iran's stockpile of approximately 1,000 pounds of enriched uranium.

Trump described the material as “nuclear dust” and said indirect negotiations with Tehran over its future were continuing.

Although much of the material is believed to be buried beneath extensive rubble from previous strikes, Trump said he was not satisfied with the prospect of it remaining there.

“Even though it’s under hundreds of tons of rock, I would say that I’m not happy that it will be there,” he told the FT.

He added that the issue remained among the subjects being discussed in ongoing contacts with Iran.

headline: US Democrats set to take House majority, wresting control from Republicans, US media projects
description: Democrats are set to win control of the US House of Representatives, flipping the chamber from Republicans, US media projected Tuesday.
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Democrats are set to win control of the US House of Representatives, flipping the chamber from Republicans, US media projected Tuesday.

All 435 House seats are up for election in the midterms, and a party needs 218 for a majority.

According to Associated Press (AP) race calls, Democrats have picked up seven Republican-held seats so far. The flips came in Kentucky's 6th District, North Carolina’s 11th District, New Jersey’s 7th District, Ohio’s 15th District and Pennsylvania’s 7th, 8th and 10th districts.

In Ohio, Democrat Don Leonard was elected in the 15th District. In Pennsylvania, Democrats Paige Cognetti and Janelle Stelson won in the 8th and 10th districts, respectively.

Republican Rep. Mike Johnson was reelected in Louisiana’s 4th District.

The projected takeover would give Democrats control of the lower chamber of Congress, giving the party greater power to shape the legislative agenda and conduct oversight of the Republican administration in the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term.

Counting continues in races across the country.

headline: Trump says he is 'absolutely willing to accept' elections results
description: US President Donald Trump said late Tuesday that he would accept the results of the midterm elections and was prepared to work with Democrats as the party
author: Anadolu
article_text:
US President Donald Trump said late Tuesday that he would accept the results of the midterm elections and was prepared to work with Democrats as the party appeared poised to take control of both chambers of Congress, according to the New York Times.

“I am absolutely willing to accept those results,” Trump told the newspaper during a phone interview while watching election returns at the White House.

“We’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out,” he added.

Trump's remarks came as Republicans faced significant setbacks in several closely watched races, with Democrats making gains that could reshape the balance of power in Washington and complicate the president's legislative agenda for the remainder of his term.

The president blamed Republican losses partly on his absence from the ballot, arguing that the party's performance might have been different had he been personally running in the elections.

headline: Kashmir Chowk underpass to open in Islamabad on Thursday
description: The Kashmir Chowk Underpass will be opened to traffic on Thursday after its construction was completed in a record 27 days, Federal Interior Minister Mohsin
author: NNI
article_text:
The Kashmir Chowk Underpass will be opened to traffic on Thursday after its construction was completed in a record 27 days, Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi announced on Wednesday.

The project also includes the plantation of 6,000 trees and plants in the surrounding area as part of efforts to improve the city's environment.

Mohsin Naqvi visited the underpass late Tuesday night to inspect the finishing work and review the project's progress. During the visit, he met the workers involved in the construction and appreciated their round-the-clock efforts.

Addressing the workers, the minister described them as the real heroes, saying their dedication and hard work had enabled the project to be completed ahead of schedule.

He also praised the quality of construction and acknowledged the efforts of the teams involved in delivering the public welfare project within a short period.

The underpass is another infrastructure project completed in Islamabad in just 27 days and is expected to facilitate traffic flow in the area following its opening.

headline: UN emissions roadmap offers narrowing window to keep global warming below 2°C
description: The world still has an opportunity to limit global warming to below 2°C, but achieving that target will require substantially deeper emissions reductions
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The world still has an opportunity to limit global warming to below 2°C, but achieving that target will require substantially deeper emissions reductions by 2035 and stronger financial support for developing economies facing growing climate risks.

Global greenhouse gas emissions would need to fall approximately 24% below 2025 levels by 2035 to keep warming below 2°C, compared with the 11–15% reductions expected under existing national climate commitments.

The gap highlights the challenge facing governments as they prepare for COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20, where stronger climate action and financial support for vulnerable countries will remain important priorities.

According to the UN Environment Programme's (UNEP) Emissions Gap Report 2026: The Point of Return, released on October 21, current policies would put the world on course for approximately 2.8°C of warming this century, while full implementation of existing national pledges would reduce the projected increase to 2.6–2.7°C.

The report also acknowledges for the first time that limiting warming to 1.5°C without temporarily exceeding that threshold is no longer possible, underscoring the importance of accelerating emissions reductions to prevent further temperature increases.

Global greenhouse gas emissions reached 58.4 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2025, remaining broadly unchanged from 2024, although emissions from fossil fuel combustion continued to increase.

By September 2026, 124 parties had submitted updated national climate commitments, but these had made only a limited difference to the projected global temperature increase.

The United States recorded the largest increase in emissions of any country in 2025, approximately 133 million tonnes, while its withdrawal from the Paris Agreement accounted for roughly half of the deterioration in the report's warming projections.

Despite these challenges, the global energy transition has recorded significant progress over the past decade.

Since 2015, renewable energy capacity has expanded approximately three times faster than the International Energy Agency had projected, while renewable sources overtook coal in global electricity generation for the first time in 2025.

Investment in clean energy is expected to reach around $2.2 trillion in 2026, nearly twice the amount being invested in fossil fuels.

However, global consumption of coal, oil and gas remains at record levels, while fossil fuel subsidies increased from approximately $660 billion in 2018 to $920 billion in 2024, complicating efforts to accelerate emissions reductions.

The implications extend beyond energy markets to economic development, food security and climate resilience, particularly in countries already exposed to extreme weather events.

According to the UNEP report, every five years of CO₂ emissions at current levels could add approximately 0.1°C to peak global warming.

Under existing policies, there is a 16–33% probability that global warming could exceed 2°C as early as 2050.

The report's pathway for returning to 1.5°C by 2100 also relies on removing approximately 320 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere during this century, a scale of carbon removal that UNEP itself considers uncertain.

For climate-vulnerable developing economies, closing the emissions gap will depend heavily on access to affordable international financing.

Dr Bakht Bilal Khan, Head of Business Development and Climate Action at WeatherWalay, told Wealth Pakistan that the global emissions gap was fundamentally linked to the availability of climate finance. He noted that G20 countries accounted for approximately 76% of global greenhouse gas emissions, while existing national commitments worldwide would reduce global emissions by only 5–8% by 2030, compared with the 18% reduction required under the more ambitious pathway.

Khan said the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities required countries with historically higher emissions to take the lead in decarbonisation and provide financial support to developing economies.

He emphasised the importance of delivering the $300 billion annual climate finance goal by 2035 through grants and concessional financing rather than adding to the debt burdens of vulnerable countries.

"Without finance, there is no ambition; without ambition, there is no 2°C," he said.

Khan added that Pakistan, which contributes less than 1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, needed access to affordable capital to accelerate its clean energy transition and avoid long-term dependence on fossil fuel infrastructure.

Aisha Khan, Chief Executive of the Civil Society Coalition for Climate Change (CSCCC) and the Mountain and Glacier Protection Organization (MGPO), said developing countries such as Pakistan should use the findings to strengthen their case for greater international financing for climate adaptation.

She also emphasised the importance of increasing support for the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, particularly as limiting global warming to 1.5°C no longer appeared to be a realistic objective without temporarily exceeding that threshold.

For vulnerable economies, stronger adaptation financing and support for addressing climate-related losses will be increasingly important as higher temperatures intensify risks to agriculture, infrastructure and livelihoods.

The UNEP roadmap indicates that limiting warming to below 2°C remains achievable, but the opportunity is narrowing as delays increase the scale and cost of future emissions reductions.

The challenge for governments heading to COP31 will be to translate climate commitments into faster emissions reductions while ensuring that developing countries receive the financial resources needed to strengthen resilience and pursue cleaner economic growth.

For countries such as Pakistan, progress on both fronts could help reduce exposure to future climate related losses while supporting a more sustainable energy transition.

Global greenhouse gas emissions would need to fall approximately 24% below 2025 levels by 2035 to keep warming below 2°C, compared with the 11–15% reductions expected under existing national climate commitments.

The gap highlights the challenge facing governments as they prepare for COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20, where stronger climate action and financial support for vulnerable countries will remain important priorities.

headline: Saddar Bairooni police arrest 2 wounded car snatchers after exchange of fire on Adiala Road
description: Rawalpindi - Two armed car snatchers were arrested in injured condition after an exchange of fire with a team of Saddar Bairooni police on Adiala Road late at
author: Mudassir Raja
article_text: Rawalpindi - Two armed car snatchers were arrested in injured condition after an exchange of fire with a team of Saddar Bairooni police on Adiala Road late at Monday night, while their third accomplice managed to escape in the darkness. In the FIR, the police said that a team of law enforcers was present at Shahpur Morr on Adiala Road at about 10:30pm when an informer told them that a white Suzuki Alto car was coming from DHA towards Shahpur Morr. The informer told the police that the car was snatched at gunpoint from the owner at Jahrahi Stop on Adiala Road a few days ago. On receiving the information, the police team called in more support from the police station and started waiting for the car. At about 10:30pm, the police noticed the car coming swiftly towards them. They signaled it to stop but the driver tried to turn back and sped away. When the police personnel tried to stop the car, three men came out of the vehicle and started straight shooting at the police team. The policemen said that they took shelter behind the official vehicle and retaliated to aerial firing in self defence. The police noticed after the shooting stopped that a man was lying on the ground and he was wounded. The law enforcers found another wounded man some yards away. The two men were identified as Jahanzeb Khan, resident of Dheri Hassanabad and Subhan Ullah, resident of Mumtaz Colony on Adiala Road. The escaped robber was identified as Sharo Khan, resident of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The police recovered illicit arms and the snatched car from the custody of the arrested robbers. Saddar Bairooni Station House Officer Raja Aizaz Azeem said that the two arrested men were also involved in an armed attack on a police party on Terbela Colony Road on November 1 night. He said that the arrested men managed to escape from the shooting site when their accomplice Umer bin Tariq alias Peru, resident of Mumtaz Market Adiala Road, was arrested from the spot with a motorcycle that was also stolen. Senior police officers rushed to the site upon receiving information about the incident. The injured suspects were shifted to the hospital for medical treatment, and police expect key revelations during their interrogation. Meanwhile, a search operation is underway in the area to track down the fleeing suspect.

headline: CPC membership exceeds 100 million, with 5.4 million grassroots organisations
description: The Communist Party of China (CPC) has more than 100 million members and over 5.4 million primary-level Party organisations, giving it an organisational
author: APP
article_text:
The Communist Party of China (CPC) has more than 100 million members and over 5.4 million primary-level Party organisations, giving it an organisational advantage unmatched by any other political party in the world, a senior official said.

Huang Jianfa, deputy head of the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee, shared the figures at a press conference explaining the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, held in Beijing from October 26 to 29.

Huang said Party organisations at all levels, along with members and officials, were responsible for ensuring full and rigorous Party self-governance and played a key role in advancing the Party's and country's development.

He said the CPC had emphasised strengthening Party building in emerging sectors through a resolution adopted at the plenary session.

The Party will expand the coverage of its organisations and activities across new types of economic and social organisations, as well as among workers engaged in emerging forms of employment, to strengthen its appeal, cohesion and influence in these sectors, he added.

New types of economic organisations include non-public-sector enterprises and businesses operating in emerging industries, while social organisations encompass industry associations, chambers of commerce, social service agencies and community-based groups.

Emerging forms of employment have developed alongside the expansion of the internet and digital economy, including food delivery couriers, ride-hailing drivers and online marketers who rely on digital platforms for work.

China currently has around 84 million people engaged in these new forms of employment. Huang said they played an important role in meeting daily needs, supporting livelihoods and sustaining economic activity.

headline: NA committee reviews export scheme, raises concerns over misuse
description: The National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue on Tuesday reviewed the performance and proposed reforms of the Export Facilitation Scheme
author: APP
article_text:
The National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue on Tuesday reviewed the performance and proposed reforms of the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS), progress on the Tajir Dost Scheme and the economic implications of border closures.

During a meeting, committee members sought a comprehensive briefing on the EFS, including its financial utilisation, operational mechanism, eligibility criteria and contribution to Pakistan’s export growth.

Members expressed concerns over the alleged misuse of the facility and questioned its effectiveness, noting that its implementation had not been accompanied by a corresponding increase in overall exports. They stressed the need to assess the scheme through verifiable data demonstrating its actual contribution to export performance.

Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani informed the committee that the EFS was designed to facilitate exporters by reducing the cost of imported raw materials used in producing goods for export.

He assured the committee that a detailed presentation covering the scheme’s performance, financial utilisation, export impact, eligibility criteria and proposed reforms would be submitted at its next meeting.

The committee also reviewed progress on the Tajir Dost Scheme and expressed concern over the lower-than-expected response from retailers despite extensive consultations with trade organisations and business representatives.

Bilal Azhar Kayani informed members that the deadline for filing returns under the scheme had expired on October 31, and the government was preparing to move towards its enforcement phase.

He explained that retailers failing to comply with the scheme would face penalties in addition to their statutory obligation to file tax returns. He reiterated the government's commitment to broadening the tax base and ensuring effective implementation.

The committee was further informed that consultations had been held with the Attorney General for Pakistan and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to ensure the legal and procedural soundness of the proposed enforcement measures.

The detailed enforcement plan would be finalised and subsequently submitted to the prime minister.

Meanwhile, the committee deferred consideration of The Companies (Amendment) Bill, 2026 until its next meeting.

The meeting was attended by MNAs Rana Iradat Sharif Khan, Syed Sami ul Hassan Gillani, Dr Mirza Ikhtiar Baig, Dr Nafisa Shah, Muhammad Jawed Hanif Khan, Shahida Begum and Dr Sharmila Sahiba Faruqui, who participated virtually.

Senior officials from the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Law and Justice, FBR and Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) also attended the meeting.

headline: Trump links midterm defeat to voter unhappiness over fuel costs during Iran war
description: Reflecting on his party's losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections, US President Donald Trump said that while voters support his posture on Iran, they
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Reflecting on his party's losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections, US President Donald Trump said that while voters support his posture on Iran, they probably were not willing to accept higher gasoline prices driven by the war.

"People agree with what I'm doing on Iran, but they really probably weren't willing to do the short-term consequence of paying ... more for gasoline," Trump told Fox News Wednesday following the midterm vote, describing the price pressure as "a short-term problem, but for long-term gain."

Trump warned that American forces could "finish the job" if Tehran fails to cooperate, though he maintained that a diplomatic agreement remains achievable if it establishes binding restrictions on nuclear weapons.

He also reiterated his decision to cut aid to Israel, saying it has "become quite rich" and no longer needs $4 billion in annual aid.

The remarks came as Democrats were projected by US media to win control of the Senate and appeared on course to secure a majority in the House of Representatives, threatening to constrain Trump's legislative agenda.

Acknowledging the outcome, Trump commended opposition candidates for fighting "hard" and said he can work with Democrats "on a lot of things," including immigration issues.

He separately told Politico that while he retains the constitutional authority to veto legislation, he prefers working with lawmakers rather than spending two years vetoing bills.

"People agree with what I'm doing on Iran, but they really probably weren't willing to do the short-term consequence of paying ... more for gasoline," Trump told Fox News Wednesday following the midterm vote, describing the price pressure as "a short-term problem, but for long-term gain."

Trump warned that American forces could "finish the job" if Tehran fails to cooperate, though he maintained that a diplomatic agreement remains achievable if it establishes binding restrictions on nuclear weapons.

He also reiterated his decision to cut aid to Israel, saying it has "become quite rich" and no longer needs $4 billion in annual aid.

The remarks came as Democrats were projected by US media to win control of the Senate and appeared on course to secure a majority in the House of Representatives, threatening to constrain Trump's legislative agenda.

Acknowledging the outcome, Trump commended opposition candidates for fighting "hard" and said he can work with Democrats "on a lot of things," including immigration issues.

He separately told Politico that while he retains the constitutional authority to veto legislation, he prefers working with lawmakers rather than spending two years vetoing bills.

headline: Legendary singer Reshma remembered on 13th death anniversary
description: ISLAMABAD - Legendary folk singer Reshma, popularly known as the “Nightingale of the Desert,” was remembered on her 13th death anniversary on
author: The Nation
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Legendary folk singer Reshma, popularly known as the “Nightingale of the Desert,” was remembered on her 13th death anniversary on Tuesday. Born in Rajasthan in 1947, Reshma migrated to Pakistan after partition and rose to prominence with her soulful voice, earning acclaim both nationally and internationally. She gained widespread recognition through her memorable songs, including “Lambi Judai,” “Hai O Rabba” and “Ankhiyan Nu Rehn De,” which continue to resonate with music lovers. In recognition of her outstanding contribution to the field of music, she was honoured with the Pride of Performance Award by the Government of Pakistan in 1982. Reshma passed away in Lahore on November 03, 2013, leaving behind a rich musical legacy that continues to inspire generations.

headline: IHC grants protective bail to TikToker ‘Mr Pattlo’ in Sialkot stampede case
description: ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) Tuesday granted protective bail to TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, alias “Mr Pattlo”, after a stampede at
author: SHAHID RAO
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) Tuesday granted protective bail to TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, alias “Mr Pattlo”, after a stampede at his mehndi (henna) event in Sialkot claimed two lives. A single bench of IHC comprising Chief Justice of IHC Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar granted the protective — also known as transitory — bail for the TikToker until November 10, allowing him to avoid arrest and directing him to approach the relevant court to seek legal remedy. Jatt surrendered himself before the court in a wheelchair. Jatt had announced holding a mehndi event and prize-distribution ceremony at Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road on Friday night; however, with hundreds gathered at the site, a stampede occurred when the stadium gates opened, killing two and injuring 18 people. Subsequently, a first information report (FIR) was registered on October 31 at the Motra police station, naming Jatt, his brother, the owner of Faraz Cricket Ground, six others, and 40-45 unidentified security guards. Jatt had filed a petition, seeking the court’s intervention to prevent his arrest before he could reach the court of competent jurisdiction. Advocates Barrister Qasim Nawaz Abbasi and Barrister Raja Ali Abbas Jalap filed the petition on his behalf. According to the legal document, Jatt was named in the FIR, which was registered under Sections 322 (punishment for qatl-i-khata), 440 (mischief committed after preparation made for causing death or hurt), 431 (mischief by injury to public road, bridge, river or channel), 148 (rioting, armed with deadly weapon), 149 (unlawful assembly), 188 (disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant) and 109 (punishment of abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), read with Section 16 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960. During the hearing, the petitioner’s counsel argued that the FIR was registered outside the IHC’s territorial jurisdiction. However, the counsel maintained that the sole object of seeking protective bail was to enable a suspect present within the jurisdiction of one court to safely approach the court where the case was registered without being arrested on the way. “The merits of the case are not required to be examined at this stage,” the petition stated, adding that without the protection, the petitioner’s right to seek pre-arrest bail before a Sialkot court would be rendered illusory. The petition further contended that the allegations levelled against the petitioner were “false, frivolous, and baseless,” claiming that he had been falsely implicated. It was also brought to the court’s notice that the petitioner had no previous criminal record and that no other petition seeking the same relief had been filed before any other court. After hearing the arguments, Justice Dogar granted the relief, noting the temporary and limited nature of the protective bail and allowing the petitioner time to surrender before the appropriate forum.
