headline: Pakistani tech founders hosted at Norway’s Parliament as Pakistan Tech Summit returns to Oslo for 16th edition
description: OSLO - Ejad Labs’ annual Pakistani tech delegation to Oslo Innovation Week was hosted at the Storting, Norway’s Parliament, by Member of Parliament
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: OSLO - Ejad Labs’ annual Pakistani tech delegation to Oslo Innovation Week was hosted at the Storting, Norway’s Parliament, by Member of Parliament Farukh Qureshi on Tuesday, 20th October, 2026. The next day, the 16th Pakistan Tech Summit drew more than 100 participants from Norway alone to Dattera til Hagen, seven years after the summit’s first edition in the same city. The Storting meeting brought around 70 Pakistani founders and Norwegian business leaders into one room. Pakistan’s Ambassador to Norway, Asim Ali Khan, who had earlier welcomed the delegation at the Embassy of Pakistan, attended. The meeting was initiated by Kristin Anderssen, CEO of Make-A-Wish Norge and a supporter of the summit since its first edition in 2019, and organised with Fredrik Syversen of TEK Norge, Norway’s technology industry association. The host MP, whose father came to Norway from Pakistan as a worker in the 1970s, said that helping to build bridges between the two countries meant something extra to him. At the summit on Wednesday, 21st October, Rehan Allahwala, Huba Rao and Jamil Rehman spoke about what it takes to build between Pakistan and Norway, from education and business culture to operating across borders. The summit was supported by Erlend Eidsvoll, Head of Special Projects at Yango. “Oslo is where this started for us, back in 2019. Coming back felt less like another event and more like a homecoming,” said Mehroz Azam, Co-founder of Ejad Labs and Future Fest. “Standing in the room where Norway’s laws are made and debated, I honestly had to pause. Seven years into building this corridor between Pakistan and Norway, the impact speaks for itself.” According to the organisers, local trade bodies now bring their own delegations to the summit and to Oslo Innovation Week. Pakistan’s digital economy is valued at over $36 billion, and more than 30,000 new software engineers join its workforce every year.

headline: PHP arrests 1,082 POs, recovers 712 stolen vehicles in October
description: LAHORE - The Punjab Highway Patrol (PHP) arrested 1,082 proclaimed offenders and court absconders and recovered 712 stolen vehicles and motorcycles during
author: Staff Reporter
article_text: LAHORE - The Punjab Highway Patrol (PHP) arrested 1,082 proclaimed offenders and court absconders and recovered 712 stolen vehicles and motorcycles during October 2026 as part of its province-wide campaign against crime and traffic violations. According to the monthly performance report released by the Punjab Highway Patrol here on Tuesday, its personnel checked 3.5 million individuals on highways through the E-Police Post App, while 1.9 million vehicles were also checked across the province. During the month, legal action was taken against 9,894 vehicles for axle-load violations, while 1,999 drivers were proceeded against for the illegal use of gas cylinders. To facilitate commuters, the PHP issued 4,829 driving licences and traced 60 missing children, reuniting them with their parents. It also removed 79 temporary and permanent encroachments from highways to improve traffic flow and provided assistance and guidance to 40,119 commuters. The report further stated that 1,947 citizens received various policing services at Police Khidmat Markaz. In action against illegal weapons, 73 cases were registered and 3 rifles, 3 guns, 59 pistols and 20,482 bullets were recovered from the possession of accused persons. During operations against drug peddlers, the PHP recovered 2,490 litres of liquor, 1,740 grams of charas, 3,800 grams of cannabis and 3,180 grams of heroin. A Punjab Police spokesperson said the PHP was utilising modern technology and effective policing strategies to prevent crime, facilitate citizens and ensure safe travel on highways across the province.

headline: Court extends physical remand of two suspects
description: LAHORE - A court on Tuesday extended the physical remand of two suspects, Fahim Akram and Naeem, by two days in a case involving an alleged Rs35 billion fraud
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - A court on Tuesday extended the physical remand of two suspects, Fahim Akram and Naeem, by two days in a case involving an alleged Rs35 billion fraud through the online sale of counterfeit US postage stamps. The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) produced the suspects before the court after the expiry of their four-day physical remand. The agency requested the court to extend the physical remand to complete the investigation. At this, the court extended the physical remand for another two days. It directed the agency to produce the suspects again on November 5. According to the NCCIA, the suspects had been operating a website under the name of “Labels Bank” since August 2023. The agency accused that the suspects had allegedly sold more than five million counterfeit US postage stamps through the website.

headline: Imposter posing as doctor arrested at LGH
description: LAHORE - The Lahore General Hospital (LGH) administration on Tuesday handed over a man to police after catching him posing as a doctor and attempting to
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The Lahore General Hospital (LGH) administration on Tuesday handed over a man to police after catching him posing as a doctor and attempting to mislead hospital staff. According to hospital officials, the accused, identified as Muhammad Anas, entered the hospital wearing a doctor’s attire and introduced himself as a doctor. The security staff took him into custody and handed him over to police following a written complaint by Security Supervisor Hafeez Baig. Police have initiated legal proceedings against him. Initial investigations revealed that the accused had allegedly defrauded a citizen by taking money in exchange for a fake employment order. Kot Lakhpat police had already registered a case against him in this regard. Meanwhile, Medical Superintendent LGH Prof Dr Faryad Hussain directed security personnel to remain vigilant and strengthen security arrangements to ensure the safety of patients and maintain discipline on the hospital premises. The hospital administration warned that strict action would be taken against anyone involved in impersonation, forgery or other unlawful activities.

headline: UCP seeks stronger academic links with Turkish universities
description: LAHORE - The University of Central Punjab (UCP) celebrated the 103rd Republic Day of Turkiye with a special ceremony held here on Tuesday. The ceremony
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - The University of Central Punjab (UCP) celebrated the 103rd Republic Day of Turkiye with a special ceremony held here on Tuesday. The ceremony highlighted the historic friendship between Pakistan and Turkiye and exploring new avenues of academic cooperation between the two countries.Turkish Consul General in Lahore Mehmet Emin Shamshek, accompanied by his wife, attended the ceremony as chief guest. Dean Professor Dr Khalid Manzoor Butt, Pro-Rector Professor Dr Hammad Naveed, Group Head of Punjab Group of Colleges Khadija Amir and other distinguished guests were also present. The university campus was decorated with the national flags of Pakistan and Turkiye, while students warmly welcomed the guests with bouquets. In his welcome address, Professor Dr Khalid Manzoor Butt highlighted the historic, cultural and brotherly ties between Pakistan and Turkiye, saying that the friendship between the two countries was founded on mutual trust and shared values.

He also underscored the importance of defence cooperation among Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. Students presented regional dances and traditional songs reflecting Pakistani culture, which were appreciated by the chief guest. The Turkish Consul General thanked the UCP administration for celebrating Turkiye’s national day with enthusiasm and warmth. In his remarks, Pro-Rector Professor Dr Hammad Naveed thanked the Consul General and his wife for attending the ceremony and presented them with commemorative shields and traditional handicrafts. Later, delegations from UCP and the Turkish Consulate discussed opportunities for joint degree programmes, student and faculty exchanges, research collaboration and enhanced academic ties. The Turkish Consul General assured his cooperation in strengthening institutional linkages between UCP and Turkish universities.

The ceremony highlighted the historic friendship between Pakistan and Turkiye and exploring new avenues of academic cooperation between the two countries.Turkish Consul General in Lahore Mehmet Emin Shamshek, accompanied by his wife, attended the ceremony as chief guest. Dean Professor Dr Khalid Manzoor Butt, Pro-Rector Professor Dr Hammad Naveed, Group Head of Punjab Group of Colleges Khadija Amir and other distinguished guests were also present. The university campus was decorated with the national flags of Pakistan and Turkiye, while students warmly welcomed the guests with bouquets. In his welcome address, Professor Dr Khalid Manzoor Butt highlighted the historic, cultural and brotherly ties between Pakistan and Turkiye, saying that the friendship between the two countries was founded on mutual trust and shared values.

He also underscored the importance of defence cooperation among Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

Students presented regional dances and traditional songs reflecting Pakistani culture, which were appreciated by the chief guest. The Turkish Consul General thanked the UCP administration for celebrating Turkiye’s national day with enthusiasm and warmth.

In his remarks, Pro-Rector Professor Dr Hammad Naveed thanked the Consul General and his wife for attending the ceremony and presented them with commemorative shields and traditional handicrafts.

Later, delegations from UCP and the Turkish Consulate discussed opportunities for joint degree programmes, student and faculty exchanges, research collaboration and enhanced academic ties. The Turkish Consul General assured his cooperation in strengthening institutional linkages between UCP and Turkish universities.

headline: Ombudsman secures Rs216m relief for 269 citizens in three months
description: OUR STAFF RE - The Office of the Ombudsman Punjab on Tuesday secured the release of outstanding dues worth Rs.216.10 million to 269 citizens across the
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: OUR STAFF RE - The Office of the Ombudsman Punjab on Tuesday secured the release of outstanding dues worth Rs.216.10 million to 269 citizens across the province in three months through timely intervention,providing them financial relief. The citizens had approached the Ombudsman Punjab after facing delays or refusal by government departments to pay their legitimate dues. Acting on their complaints,the Ombudsman Punjab directed the relevant departments to release the outstanding amounts. According to a spokesperson,80 citizens received Rs.89.459 million as financial assistance while Rs.26.739 million was paid to 30 citizens against contractual dues. Similarly,16 citizens received Rs.37 million in pension benefits while eight were paid Rs.2.915 million as family pension. Moreover,40 citizens received Rs10.955 million as marriage grants while 10 were paid Rs.5.798 million as death grants. An amount of Rs.5.219 million was released to 23 citizens under the General Provident Fund (GP Fund) while 55 citizens received Rs.36.758 million in outstanding salaries. The payments also included Rs.239,400 in property tax refunds to three citizens and Rs.113,400 in farewell grants to two citizens. Additionally, one citizen received Rs.923,000 in group insurance, while another was paid Rs.750,000 as gratuity. The complainants appreciated the Ombudsman Punjab’s intervention, saying it helped them secure their legitimate dues and resolve their grievances.

headline: Punjab launches ‘Chamkta Lahore’ campaign to combat smog
description: LAHORE - On the direction of Chief Minister(CM), Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the provincial government on Tuesday launched a cleanliness and anti-smog drive
author: Staff Reporter
article_text: LAHORE - On the direction of Chief Minister(CM), Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the provincial government on Tuesday launched a cleanliness and anti-smog drive “Chamkta Lahore’’ aimed at improving sanitation, reducing airborne dust and ensuring cleaner roads and public spaces across the provincial capital. Minister for Local Government, Zeeshan Rafique inaugurated the campaign at a ceremony held at Liberty Chowk. Special Assistant to the CM Shoaib Mirza, Deputy Commissioner (DC), Ali Ijaz and the Chief Executive Officer(CEO) of the Lahore Waste Management Company (LWMC) were also present. Zeeshan Rafique and Shoaib Mirza operated anti-smog mist guns and reviewed their functioning. Speaking to the media, Zeeshan Rafique said the initiative had been launched under the chief minister’s vision of a clean Punjab. He said anti-smog measures introduced by the provincial government over the past two years had produced encouraging results, adding that smog levels in November were noticeably lower than those recorded two years ago. He said the provision of 10 anti-smog mist guns was a key feature of the “Chamkta Lahore” campaign. Mounted on rickshaws, these cost-effective machines would spray water into the air to suppress dust particles and complement the city’s road-washing operations. The minister said the campaign would focus on ensuring comprehensive cleanliness along major roads, busy thoroughfares and commercial areas. Initially,100 major roads, locations and commercial markets have been identified for targeted cleaning operations, he added. Under the campaign, approximately 648 kilometers of roads will be washed every week, with a daily target of 100 kilometers. Sixteen mechanical washing machines will be deployed for road cleaning while 46 rickshaw-mounted washers will be used to clean footpaths. Zeeshan Rafique expressed confidence that the initiative would make Lahore cleaner and contribute to efforts to combat smog and improve air quality. Highlighting the provincial government’s development initiatives,he said Punjab was making progress under the leadership of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. He pointed to ongoing projects in road infrastructure, healthcare, education and urban beautification, saying development activities were being carried out from major cities to union councils across the province. He added that the government’s public welfare initiatives and development projects were aimed at improving people’s quality of life. Special Assistant to CM Shoaib Mirza praised the efforts of sanitation workers, describing them as heroes whose hard work was instrumental in maintaining cleanliness. He said the chief minister’s initiative would be extended to all districts to ensure its benefits reached people across the province. The provincial government expects the campaign to strengthen urban sanitation efforts while supporting its broader strategy to address air pollution and smog,he further said.

headline: Over 456,000 children administered polio drops on first day
description: LAHORE - More than 456,000 children were administered polio vaccine on the first day of the ongoing anti-polio campaign in Lahore, while vaccination teams
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - More than 456,000 children were administered polio vaccine on the first day of the ongoing anti-polio campaign in Lahore, while vaccination teams reached 295,151 households across the city. The progress of the campaign was reviewed at a meeting chaired by Deputy Commissioner Lahore Muhammad Ali Ijaz, who directed the relevant departments to ensure 100 per cent coverage and effectively address all missed and refusal cases. Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Health Dr Asif Arbab Khan briefed the meeting on the campaign’s first-day performance. Additional Deputy Commissioner (Municipal Services), assistant commissioners and Union Council Medical Officers (UCMOs) also attended the meeting. He also instructed the teams to address parents’ concerns through effective communication and complete vaccination of all eligible children. Emphasising the importance of maintaining the cold chain, he directed the health authorities to ensure proper storage and handling of polio vaccines throughout the campaign.

DC Muhammad Ali Ijaz said polio eradication was a national responsibility and, in line with the vision of Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif, all-out efforts would be made to ensure a polio-free Punjab. He said there was no room for negligence in the anti-polio campaign and directed the officials to adopt an effective strategy to cover refusal cases. He also urged parents to cooperate with vaccination teams and ensure that their children received polio drops.

Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Health Dr Asif Arbab Khan briefed the meeting on the campaign’s first-day performance. Additional Deputy Commissioner (Municipal Services), assistant commissioners and Union Council Medical Officers (UCMOs) also attended the meeting. He also instructed the teams to address parents’ concerns through effective communication and complete vaccination of all eligible children. Emphasising the importance of maintaining the cold chain, he directed the health authorities to ensure proper storage and handling of polio vaccines throughout the campaign.

DC Muhammad Ali Ijaz said polio eradication was a national responsibility and, in line with the vision of Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif, all-out efforts would be made to ensure a polio-free Punjab.

He said there was no room for negligence in the anti-polio campaign and directed the officials to adopt an effective strategy to cover refusal cases. He also urged parents to cooperate with vaccination teams and ensure that their children received polio drops.

headline: Faryal Talpur to visit Lahore ahead of LG elections
description: LAHORE - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Women’s Wing Central President Faryal Talpur is expected to visit Lahore on November 10 or 11 for approximately a
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Women’s Wing Central President Faryal Talpur is expected to visit Lahore on November 10 or 11 for approximately a week as the party intensifies preparations for the upcoming local government elections in Punjab. The PPP Lahore has planned a grand reception for Ms Talpur, with party leaders, office-bearers and workers expected to participate in welcoming her, according to a press release issued on Tuesday. PPP Lahore President Faisal Mir and nominated Secretary Information Majid Ghori said the visit would mark a new phase in the party’s organisational and political activities in Punjab. They said Ms Talpur would be briefed on preparations for the local government elections, candidate selection, organisational matters and the party’s electoral strategy. The briefing would also cover the performance of local party organisations, electoral preparations in Lahore and other districts, and the status of prospective candidates. Meetings with party ticket holders, prospective candidates and workers intending to contest the local government elections would also be part of her visit. The PPP leaders said the visit aimed to strengthen the party at the grassroots level and mobilise its workers for an effective electoral campaign across Punjab. They added that the party leadership and workers would jointly formulate a comprehensive strategy to enhance the PPP’s political presence in Lahore and other districts, with a focus on public outreach and organisational mobilisation. The PPP has vowed to actively participate in the upcoming local government elections and strengthen its organisation across the province, the press release said.

headline: Punjab CM Maryam inaugurates development projects in Attock
description: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif inaugurated 127 development projects in Attock, including 59 road construction and rehabilitation schemes
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif inaugurated 127 development projects in Attock, including 59 road construction and rehabilitation schemes worth Rs 23 billion, during her visit to the district on Tuesday. The inaugurated projects also included an Agri Mall, Land Record Centre, Model Children’s Home and Fateh Jang Special Education Centre, said a handout issued here. The 59 road schemes included Fateh Jang–Pindi Gheb Road, Dhok Lahm Jhamat Road and Mithial Chowk–Dhok Pathan Road, besides several other roads. The chief minister received a warm welcome upon her arrival as a large number of people, party workers and children gathered along roads and streets to greet her. Flowers were showered along various routes and intersections, while her vehicle was covered with rose petals along Hattian Road, Kamra Road and University Road. Separately, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif distributed laptops and Honhaar scholarships among students at a ceremony held at COMSATS University, Attock, on Tuesday, with students from Swabi, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, also benefiting from the education support initiatives. Students from KP appreciated the Punjab government for extending the scholarship programme beyond provincial boundaries, saying the financial assistance had enabled them to pay semester fees amounting to nearly Rs200,000, said a handout issued here. At the ceremony, the chief minister distributed laptops and scholarship cheques among students. She was also presented with portraits and sketches prepared by students. A total of 6,161 laptops were distributed among students across the Rawalpindi division. These included 628 laptops for public university students, 257 for private university students, 461 for medical colleges, 375 for nursing colleges, 17 for special education institutions and 423 for colleges under the Higher Education Department. Under the Honhaar Scholarship Programme, 2,590 scholarships worth Rs196.97 million were awarded to students in the Rawalpindi division. Of these, 2,085 scholarships worth Rs170.21 million were allocated to students of public universities, while 314 scholarships worth Rs19.8 million went to students of medical universities and colleges. Another 191 scholarships worth Rs6.96 million were awarded to students of HED colleges. The programme covers students enrolled in public and private universities, federally chartered universities, BS colleges, special education institutions, and medical and dental colleges. The chief minister has increased the number of laptops allocated for deserving students from 40,000 to 112,000. So far, 48,292 laptops have been distributed among students in different districts of Punjab. Under the first three phases of the Honhaar Scholarship Programme, 108,000 students have received scholarships. The ceremony was attended by elected representatives, party ticket-holders and other political leaders, whom the chief minister also met on the occasion.

headline: 225,000 loans disbursed under Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar scheme
description: LAHORE - More than 128,000 houses have been completed under Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif’s Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar programme with the
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - More than 128,000 houses have been completed under Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif’s Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar programme with the government recovering 97.6 percent of loan instalments amounting to Rs22.29 billion, according to a handout. A special meeting chaired by the chief minister reviewed progress on the housing initiative, which has attracted more than 1.7 million registrations since its launch. The meeting was informed that over 225,000 loans had been disbursed under the scheme, while 128,718 houses had been completed. Another 62,600 houses were nearing completion, and 171,597 beneficiaries had received the second instalment of their loans. The briefing highlighted a loan recovery rate of 97.6 per cent, with Rs22.29 billion recovered in instalments from beneficiaries. Maryam Nawaz approved inviting fresh applications for the Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar scheme and directed the authorities to ensure timely achievement of its completion targets. The meeting was also briefed on the Apni Chhat, Mehfooz Chhat initiative, for which the application process has been completed. Under the programme, 3,055 applicants have received loans worth Rs1.216 billion, while construction and expansion work on 532 houses has been completed. The chief minister directed the relevant authorities to ensure that all targets under the housing initiatives were achieved within the stipulated timelines.

headline: Russia offers scholarships to international students through Open Doors Olympiad
description: Russia offers scholarships to international students through the Open Doors Olympiad, covering travel, accommodation, health insurance and a monthly stipend.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
International students seeking higher education opportunities in Russia can apply for a scholarship programme offered by the Russian Federation through the International Open Doors Olympiad.

The programme provides financial assistance to eligible students who secure admission to Russian universities after winning or obtaining a qualifying position in the international competition.

Successful candidates will receive financial support throughout their studies in Russia, from their arrival in the country until graduation.

The scholarship covers travel expenses, health insurance and accommodation costs, along with a monthly stipend exceeding 27,000 roubles.

The initiative aims to attract talented students from across the world who meet the eligibility requirements established under the International Open Doors Olympiad.

Further details regarding eligibility criteria, application procedures and scholarship benefits are available on the programme's official website.

headline: PFA fines 150 food businesses Rs1.825m in Sialkot
description: The Punjab Food Authority (PFA) inspected 1,708 food businesses in Sialkot during October and imposed fines amounting to Rs1.825 million on 150 units for
author: NNI
article_text:
The Punjab Food Authority (PFA) inspected 1,708 food businesses in Sialkot during October and imposed fines amounting to Rs1.825 million on 150 units for violating food safety regulations.

According to a PFA spokesperson, production at five food outlets was suspended due to unhygienic conditions, while eight food samples were collected for laboratory analysis.

During the inspection campaign, the authority also discarded adulterated spices, substandard vinegar, spoiled meat, Chinese salt and other prohibited ingredients.

The spokesperson said 613 food businesses were issued improvement notices over various violations, including poor cleanliness, the presence of insects in production areas and failure to maintain mandatory records.

PFA Director General Mansoor Ahmed said food adulteration was a serious offence and urged citizens to purchase PFA-approved food products in properly sealed and packaged containers.

headline: KP governor, PM’s aide discuss digital media cooperation
description: Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi met Minister of State and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Digital Media Fahd Haroon at his residence
author: NNI
article_text:
Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi met Minister of State and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Digital Media Fahd Haroon at his residence on Wednesday to discuss the prevailing national situation, digital media and matters of mutual interest.

During the meeting, the two leaders exchanged views on the evolving digital media landscape and the growing role of technology in strengthening public communication and engagement.

They also discussed broader issues relating to public communication, institutional engagement and areas of mutual interest.

Both leaders appreciated the exchange of views and expressed their commitment to maintaining continued engagement and cooperation.

headline: Hailey Bieber opens up about health battle following son Jack's birth
description: Hailey Bieber opens up about experiencing PMDD after welcoming son Jack Blues, discusses her past mini stroke and highlights the need for women's health
author: Web Entertainment Desk
article_text:
Hailey Bieber has revealed that she experienced premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) following the birth of her son, Jack Blues, highlighting the importance of open conversations about women's health.

The founder of beauty brand Rhode, who is married to singer Justin Bieber, told Women's Wear Daily (WWD) that she struggled with the condition after welcoming her son in August 2024.

"After I had my son, I struggled with [PMDD] a bit, and there's just not a lot of conversation or research around it," she said.

PMDD is a severe form of premenstrual syndrome (PMS), with symptoms that can include anxiety, panic attacks, depression, insomnia, fatigue and mood swings.

Explaining her decision to speak publicly about the condition, Bieber said discussing such experiences could help others feel less isolated.

She said greater openness about women's health issues "makes it feel like less of a lonely journey."

Her remarks follow earlier disclosures about her health during an appearance on the Therapuss podcast this year.

Bieber recalled suffering a "mini stroke" in 2022, describing the experience as a serious medical emergency.

"A couple of years ago, I had a crazy medical situation," she said.

She also revealed that she was born with a congenital heart defect known as patent foramen ovale, which required a medical procedure performed through the groin.

According to Bieber, the procedure allowed her to return home the same day.

She said the experience had made her "hyper aware" of her body and contributed to feelings of anxiety about her health.

Bieber also linked her interest in health and medicine to the inspiration behind her beauty brand, Rhode.

The company has pledged $5 million over three years to the Foundation for Women's Health to support research into women's health issues.

Bieber sold Rhode to e.l.f. Beauty in 2025 in a deal valued at $1 billion.

headline: CM Bugti directs accelerated completion of Safe City projects across Balochistan
description: Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti on Wednesday chaired the 29th meeting of the Hardening of the State Committee to review the province's security
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti on Wednesday chaired the 29th meeting of the Hardening of the State Committee to review the province's security situation, development projects and measures to curb illegal activities.

The meeting was attended by representatives of federal and provincial institutions, relevant government departments and security forces.

Participants discussed measures to prevent smuggling, drug trafficking, poppy cultivation and other unlawful activities, emphasising the need to intensify operations against such practices across the province.

The meeting also reviewed progress on the conversion of B-Areas into A-Areas. Participants expressed satisfaction with the ongoing process and reaffirmed their commitment to extending it effectively across all divisions.

During the meeting, the chief minister directed the provision of necessary funds and resources to ensure the timely completion of Safe City projects in Quetta and other major cities of the province.

The participants reiterated their resolve to strengthen coordination among relevant institutions to maintain law and order, ensure lasting peace, uphold the rule of law and reinforce the writ of the state across Balochistan.

headline: Muslim candidates make historic gains in US midterm elections
description: Several Muslim candidates have secured significant victories in the US midterm elections, strengthening Muslim representation in Congress and other legislative
author: NNI
article_text:
Several Muslim candidates have secured significant victories in the US midterm elections, strengthening Muslim representation in Congress and other legislative institutions.

According to unofficial preliminary results reported by US media, incumbent Democratic Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib was re-elected from Michigan, while Ilhan Omar secured another term representing Minnesota's Fifth Congressional District.

Omar received 62.77 per cent of the vote, defeating Republican candidate John Nagel, who secured 28.31 per cent, according to the reported results.

Other Muslim candidates also secured victories. Latifa Simon won a congressional seat in California, while Afghan-American candidate Ayesha Wahab also won her election in the state.

In Michigan, Egyptian-American Democratic candidate Dr Abdul El-Sayed was elected to the US Senate, becoming the first Muslim senator in American history, according to the report.

Meanwhile, Abr Kwas became the first Palestinian-American elected to the New York Senate, with support from New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Dr Adam Hashim Hamawi, who had treated children from Gaza, also won a congressional seat in New Jersey after defeating a Republican candidate.

The victories mark a significant development in Muslim and immigrant representation in American political institutions.

Category: World News / International Politics

headline: ECP appoints 17 officers to monitor Islamabad local elections
description: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has appointed 17 officers, including a District Monitoring Officer (DMO), to monitor compliance with the code of
author: APP
article_text:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has appointed 17 officers, including a District Monitoring Officer (DMO), to monitor compliance with the code of conduct during the December 20 local government elections in Islamabad.

According to a notification issued on Wednesday, Additional Deputy Commissioner Uzair Ali Khan has been appointed as the DMO, while 16 other officers have been assigned monitoring responsibilities across different groups of union councils in the federal capital.

The monitoring officers will oversee electoral activities in their respective areas, identify violations of the code of conduct and report them to the DMO.

The ECP has also issued terms of reference (ToRs) for the DMO and monitoring officers, requiring them to take an oath under Section 56 of the Elections Act before assuming their responsibilities.

Under the guidelines, monitoring teams will obtain information from the district administration regarding public meetings, rallies and other political activities. The district administration and relevant authorities will be required to provide necessary information and assistance.

Any violation of the code of conduct will be reported to the DMO through Form M-1 along with supporting evidence.

The local administration will appoint a Grade 17 or above officer as a focal person, while police authorities will ensure security for the monitoring teams.

The DMO will maintain a record of complaints received through Form M-2 and submit daily reports to the ECP. The monitoring teams will oversee pre-election activities, polling-day proceedings and post-election developments to ensure compliance with electoral regulations.

The DMO will also be authorised to issue directions to relevant authorities in connection with monitoring responsibilities.

Polling for Islamabad's local government elections is scheduled for December 20.

headline: Six Months of Record-Breaking Development: Union Town Offers Fully Developed, Possession-Ready Plots on Pine Avenue
description: Union Town, an LDA-approved, master-planned community developed by Union Developers (Pvt.) Limited, has achieved significant development milestones, with major
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Union Town, an LDA-approved, master-planned community developed by Union Developers (Pvt.) Limited, has achieved significant development milestones, with major infrastructure works completed and residential and commercial plots ready for possession.

Ideally located in the Heart of Urban Lahore, Union Town offers triple access via Kadir Topbas Chowk, Abdul Sattar Edhi Road, and Khayaban-e-Jinnah, ensuring seamless connectivity to key areas of the city.

Its position within the city places key landmarks within minutes' drive, including: 2 minutes to M2 Motorway, 3 minutes to Shaukat Khanum Hospital & UCP, while just 5 minutes to Lahore Ring Road and Canal Road.

Within 6 months of record-breaking development, Union Town has witnessed record-breaking progress, marked by the completion of infrastructure works, including internal road networks, streetlights, and the installation of a sewerage system.

A key feature of the community is its 150-feet-wide Pine Avenue, a signal-free corridor that runs directly through Union Town, providing access to every block. Alongside its possession-ready residential plots, Union Town offers fully developed commercials facing Pine Avenue, creating opportunities for retail, commercial activities, and business investment within a growing urban community.

Union Town reflects Union Developers' commitment to delivering well-planned communities that combine residential and commercial opportunities under its vision of Buland Mayar-e-Zindagi.

Speaking about the project's vision, Naeem Ahmad Malik, CEO of Union Developers, said, “Union Town reflects our commitment to delivering a quality lifestyle through thoughtful planning, modern infrastructure, and a community designed to serve generations to come.” With residential plots ranging from 3 to 20 Marla and commercial plots from 2 to 10 Marla, Union Town offers opportunities for people from different walks of life, creating a setting that caters to diverse lifestyle needs and investment aspirations.

With fully developed infrastructure, possession-ready plots, community parks and signal-free Pine Avenue, Union Town becomes the only kind of community that not only enhances present needs but guarantees a successful future tomorrow. https://www.uniondevelopers.com/

headline: Falak Shakeel Khan Focuses on Making Social Media and Digital Technology Easier to Understand
description: As social media continues to shape the way people communicate, work and share information, understanding how digital platforms operate has become increasingly
author: Web Desk
article_text:
As social media continues to shape the way people communicate, work and share information, understanding how digital platforms operate has become increasingly important. From account security and verification to monetisation and platform settings, users regularly encounter issues that can be difficult to resolve without clear guidance.

Falak Shakeel Khan is a digital content creator from Chhidru, Mianwali, Pakistan, currently based in Qatar. Through self-learning and practical experience, he has developed an interest in social media platforms and the everyday technical challenges faced by their users.

His content mainly covers Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube. Rather than focusing on technical explanations, he aims to make information accessible by explaining platform features, account settings and common procedures in straightforward language.

A key part of his work involves helping users understand account management and security. His tutorials also cover verification processes, monetisation features, privacy settings and changes introduced by social media platforms. These subjects are particularly relevant to people who use social media for personal communication, content creation or business purposes.

Falak shares his educational content through his YouTube channel, Falak Shakeel Tricks. The channel provides tutorials and practical information for viewers looking to understand digital services and navigate common online challenges.

One of the challenges facing social media users is keeping up with frequent platform updates. Features, policies and security requirements can change over time, sometimes leaving users unsure about the correct procedures. Through his content, Falak aims to explain these developments and provide information that viewers can use when managing their accounts.

His approach is based on simplicity and practical learning. By breaking down technical topics into understandable steps, he seeks to make digital information more accessible, particularly for people who have limited experience with technology.

As the use of online platforms continues to expand, digital awareness has become an important part of everyday life. Falak Shakeel Khan's work reflects an interest in helping people better understand social media tools, stay informed about platform changes and use digital services with greater confidence.

Through his continued interest in technology and educational content, he hopes to make everyday digital tasks easier to understand for a wider audience.

headline: Pakistan, China urged to promote shared Silk Road heritage among youth
description: Pakistan and China have been urged to strengthen efforts to promote their shared cultural heritage and historical links through the ancient Silk Road, with a
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan and China have been urged to strengthen efforts to promote their shared cultural heritage and historical links through the ancient Silk Road, with a focus on raising awareness among younger generations.

Muhammad Zamir Assadi, Research Fellow at the China International Press Communication Center (CIPCC), made the call while speaking on the sidelines of an international cultural exhibition on Wednesday.

He said highlighting historical and cultural similarities between the two countries was essential to connecting young people with their common past and encouraging them to preserve their shared heritage for future generations.

Assadi noted that several artefacts displayed at the exhibition resembled those preserved at Pakistan's Taxila Museum, reflecting centuries-old cultural exchanges between the two regions.

He said the ancient Silk Road had served as a major link between Pakistan and China, facilitating the exchange of ideas, art and cultural traditions.

According to UNESCO, Taxila was located along a branch of the Silk Road connecting China with the West, while artworks at China's Mogao Caves also reflected influences from the Gandhara civilisation.

Highlighting Pakistan's archaeological potential, Assadi said the country had a rich heritage to showcase internationally, including Gandhara civilisation sites in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and historic monuments in Lahore.

He also highlighted government efforts to promote heritage-based tourism, noting that a task force had been established in July to advance tourism linked to the Gandhara heritage.

Emphasising the role of young people, he said the younger generation could become custodians of the shared cultural legacy by developing a deeper understanding of history and cultural values.

He also encouraged Chinese visitors to explore Pakistan's archaeological heritage, discover cultural similarities between the two countries and witness ongoing efforts to preserve historic sites and artefacts.

headline: Fuel subsidy to continue until December, says PM Shehbaz
description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Wednesday that the government had shielded the public from the impact of rising energy prices and would continue its fuel
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Wednesday that the government had shielded the public from the impact of rising energy prices and would continue its fuel subsidy programme until the end of December.

Chairing a meeting of the federal cabinet, the prime minister said Pakistan was making sincere efforts to promote peace and stability in the region. He noted that Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir had visited Iran, while representatives of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye had also held talks with the Iranian leadership in Tehran. He described the discussions as taking place in a cordial and positive atmosphere.

Shehbaz said the sharp rise in international oil prices had contributed to regional instability. However, he maintained that the government had taken steps to prevent higher energy costs from placing an additional burden on ordinary citizens.

He said the fuel subsidy programme had directly benefited more than 15 million people, with Rs28 billion allocated for the initiative. The scheme would remain in place until the end of December. He added that consumers had also been protected from a Rs15-per-litre increase in petrol prices.

The prime minister said the petroleum minister and his team had held discussions with refineries to manage the impact of rising prices. He warned that petrol pumps failing to cooperate with the subsidy programme would face action.

Referring to reforms in the energy sector, Shehbaz said the era of the "LNG mafia" had come to an end, adding that the government was now relying on competition and transparency. He said state-owned companies, including Pakistan State Oil (PSO) and Pakistan Refinery Limited (PARCO), were playing a role in managing the sector, while a mechanism had also been introduced for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

With winter approaching, he said the government was working to maintain adequate supplies of liquefied natural gas (LNG), LPG and oil to meet the country's energy requirements.

The prime minister also referred to a Rs160 billion development package for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, aimed at supporting peace and development in the province. He said restoring stability in the region remained a key government priority and reiterated the commitment to eliminating terrorism.

Shehbaz acknowledged the sacrifices made by the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in the fight against militancy. He said terrorism had been eliminated from the country in 2018 but had unfortunately resurfaced.

The prime minister also congratulated Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on assuming the chairmanship of the Group of 24 (G24).

headline: Mustafa Kamal launches Care1166 system to address public health complaints
description: Federal Minister for National Health Services Syed Mustafa Kamal on Wednesday inaugurated the Care1166 Health Complaint Management System at the Federal
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for National Health Services Syed Mustafa Kamal on Wednesday inaugurated the Care1166 Health Complaint Management System at the Federal Directorate of Immunization (FDI), introducing a centralised digital platform to register public grievances and improve accountability in the health sector.

The new initiative will allow residents of Islamabad to lodge complaints about the Ministry of National Health Services and its attached departments and institutions through a single helpline, 1166, eliminating the need to visit multiple government offices.

The platform is intended to make it easier for citizens, particularly those in remote areas, to contact the relevant authorities by phone and have their health-related concerns formally recorded for action.

According to the ministry, complaints submitted through the system will be automatically referred to the relevant department or designated officer. Their progress will then be tracked from registration through to resolution.

A central dashboard has also been introduced to record each complaint, identify the officer responsible for handling it and document the steps taken to address the issue.

The health minister will have access to the dashboard from his office, allowing him to review complaints and monitor how relevant departments are responding to public concerns.

Beyond registering grievances, the system is designed to ensure that complaints receive proper follow-up and that authorities' efforts to resolve them can be monitored.

The ministry said the data collected through the platform could also help identify recurring healthcare problems and disease trends in different areas by analysing complaints received from the public.

In its initial phase, the system will cover complaints concerning government hospitals and dispensaries in Islamabad. Designated officers at the respective facilities will be responsible for ensuring that grievances are addressed promptly.

The platform will maintain a centralised, traceable record of complaints related to hospitals, enabling the Ministry of Health to monitor public feedback and service delivery across government healthcare facilities.

The ministry said the initiative was expected to be particularly beneficial for women, low-income households and marginalised communities by giving them a more accessible way to raise concerns directly with government authorities.

The system is expected to promote transparency, improve institutional accountability and help the government assess the quality of public healthcare services through the systematic monitoring of complaints and their resolution.

headline: Federal cabinet delegates CM office powers to KP governor during emergency
description: The federal cabinet on Wednesday approved the transfer of the Chief Minister’s Office powers to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to manage routine
author: APP
article_text:
The federal cabinet on Wednesday approved the transfer of the Chief Minister’s Office powers to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to manage routine administrative affairs during the state of emergency in the province.

The meeting, chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, approved the arrangement to ensure the smooth functioning of government matters and improve administrative coordination.

Under the decision, the governor will submit a monthly report to the federal government outlining how the delegated powers have been exercised.

“The Governor will submit a monthly review report to the Federal Government regarding the exercise of these delegated powers. The cabinet welcomed the decision, expressing hope that the KP Advisory Council, under the Governor’s leadership, will make all out efforts to ensure public welfare, prosperity and the restoration of law and order in the province,” the PM Office Media Wing said in a press release.

The cabinet also approved new designs for a series of currency notes on the recommendation of the Ministry of Finance.

During a briefing, the meeting was informed that artists and designers from across the country had been invited to submit designs. The process followed consultations with relevant stakeholders by a cabinet committee constituted by the prime minister.

The proposed banknotes will feature upgraded security measures and advanced materials to prevent counterfeiting and improve their durability. The cabinet also approved the introduction of a Rs10 coin to replace the existing Rs10 banknote.

In another decision, the federal cabinet ratified the defence cooperation agreement between Pakistan and Kuwait. The agreement, aimed at strengthening bilateral defence ties, was initially signed on June 11, 2023, and subsequently ratified by the Kuwaiti government on July 19.

The meeting also endorsed decisions taken by the Cabinet Committee on State-Owned Enterprises (CCOSOEs) during its October 26 meeting.

Furthermore, the cabinet ratified decisions made by the Cabinet Committee on Legislative Cases (CCLC) at meetings held on January 22, February 26, August 5, 18 and 27, as well as September 11 and 22.

headline: Pakistan, UK raise concern over terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan
description: Pakistan and the United Kingdom on Wednesday voiced concern over the continued threat from terrorist organisations operating in and from Afghanistan, according
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan and the United Kingdom on Wednesday voiced concern over the continued threat from terrorist organisations operating in and from Afghanistan, according to the Foreign Office.

The two countries held their annual counter-terrorism dialogue in Islamabad, where they reviewed bilateral and multilateral cooperation and renewed their commitment to tackling terrorism in all its forms.

During the discussions, both sides examined the changing regional and international security landscape, including threats from terrorist groups and transnational networks.

They expressed particular concern over organisations such as the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which they said were operating in and from Afghanistan. The delegations also emphasised the need for a peaceful, stable and secure Afghanistan to support lasting regional peace and prosperity.

The UK delegation offered condolences over the loss of innocent lives in terrorist attacks in Pakistan and reaffirmed Britain's support for the country in its efforts to combat terrorism.

The talks also covered the exchange of expertise and the possibility of expanding cooperation against emerging security challenges. These included misinformation and disinformation campaigns, the misuse of social media platforms and the exploitation of new technologies.

According to the Foreign Office, both countries recognised Pakistan's contributions to regional peace and security and agreed to deepen institutional cooperation through regular engagement on shared counter-terrorism priorities.

The delegations also agreed to hold the next round of talks in London in 2027, with dates to be finalised through mutual consultation.

headline: Government to compensate victims of One Constitution Avenue irregularities, says Ahsan Iqbal
description: The government will compensate those affected by alleged irregularities in the One Constitution Avenue project, Federal Minister for Planning and Development
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The government will compensate those affected by alleged irregularities in the One Constitution Avenue project, Federal Minister for Planning and Development Ahsan Iqbal said on Wednesday.

Speaking at a press conference alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, Iqbal said the federal cabinet had approved the findings of a committee tasked with investigating alleged fraud in the project.

He said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had constituted the committee to look into the matter, adding that its report had also recommended renaming the project.

According to Iqbal, the name One Constitution Avenue had itself allegedly been acquired through fraudulent means.

The planning minister said several rules and regulations had been disregarded during the project's development, while the Capital Development Authority (CDA) had also failed to properly discharge its responsibilities.

He said the government would ensure that all legal requirements were met. Iqbal also noted that the first building on Constitution Avenue housed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said people had suffered financial losses due to alleged wrongdoing and facilitation in the project. He added that the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) had been given three months to prepare a reference in the case.

"Those who were defrauded are not at fault," Chaudhry said.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the joint investigation team (JIT) had recommended referring the matter to NAB for further investigation. He added that the bureau would examine the case on merit.

headline: Pakistan, Turkmenistan seek stronger academic ties through new education initiatives
description: Pakistan and Turkmenistan have agreed to expand cooperation in higher education, Urdu language teaching, curriculum development and institutional partnerships.
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan and Turkmenistan have agreed to expand cooperation in higher education, Urdu language teaching, curriculum development and institutional partnerships.

Chairman of the Higher Education Commission (HEC), Prof. Dr. Niaz Ahmad Akhtar, met Turkmenistan's Ambassador to Pakistan, Atadjan Movlamov, at the HEC Secretariat in Islamabad to discuss ways of strengthening academic links between the two countries.

A key topic was a proposed memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the National University of Modern Languages (NUML), Islamabad, and the Dovletmammet Azadi Turkmen National Institute of World Languages in Ashgabat. Under the proposed arrangement, Pakistan would provide Urdu language teachers to the Turkmen institution to support Urdu learning and promote cultural and people-to-people exchanges.

The meeting also discussed a proposed partnership between Arkadag Islamic University and the International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI). The initiative follows a recent visit to Pakistan by former Mufti of Turkmenistan Yalkap Hojagulyyev and is aimed at expanding collaboration in Islamic studies, research, faculty exchanges and academic programmes.

Prof. Akhtar reaffirmed the HEC's support for facilitating partnerships between NUML and other Pakistani universities and their counterparts in Turkmenistan. He said the commission was ready to assist with Urdu language instruction, curriculum development and broader academic cooperation.

He also highlighted Pakistan's longstanding ties with Turkmenistan, saying the country valued its historic relationship with the Central Asian state and sought to strengthen it through educational diplomacy.

Both sides expressed their resolve to deepen cooperation in education, religious scholarship, research and cultural exchanges, building on the longstanding ties between the two countries.

headline: Ishaq Dar, Iranian envoy discuss bilateral ties and regional developments
description: Iranian Ambassador to Pakistan met Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday to discuss bilateral relations and issues of mutual
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Iranian Ambassador to Pakistan met Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday to discuss bilateral relations and issues of mutual interest, the Foreign Office said.

According to the Foreign Office spokesperson, Dar reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening its relationship with Iran.

The two sides also held detailed discussions on the regional situation and exchanged views on recent developments and matters of shared concern.

Emphasising the need for peaceful engagement, Dar highlighted the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in promoting stability and addressing regional challenges.

The meeting reflected Pakistan’s continued diplomatic engagement with Iran and its efforts to expand bilateral cooperation amid evolving regional developments.

Separately, Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei commented on the outcome of the US midterm elections, saying that changes in political leadership in Washington would not lead to a shift in what he described as America’s hostile policy towards Tehran.

In a statement, Khamenei said those expecting a change in US policy following a change of political parties were mistaken.

He further argued that people who believed American hostility could be brought to an end through concessions were holding a serious misconception.

Khamenei also warned Washington against further aggression, saying Iran would respond on a much broader scale if the United States launched another attack.

headline: Punjab CM inaugurates retired soldier’s home under Apni Chhat Apna Ghar scheme
description: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Wednesday formally inaugurated a house constructed by retired Havaldar Itbar Shah under the provincial government’s
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Wednesday formally inaugurated a house constructed by retired Havaldar Itbar Shah under the provincial government’s Apni Chhat Apna Ghar programme and congratulated his family on becoming homeowners.

During her visit, Itbar Shah shared how the initiative had helped him turn his long-held dream of owning a home into reality. He said that although he already had a plot, he had been waiting for financial support to begin construction.

The retired soldier said the government provided him with a loan of Rs1.5 million, enabling him to build a house for his family.

To mark the occasion, the chief minister presented gifts to the retired havaldar and his family. She also expressed her wish to share a meal with them.

In a statement, Maryam Nawaz expressed satisfaction over the programme achieving its target of providing 225,000 loans. She described the Apni Chhat Apna Ghar scheme as a source of hope for families across Punjab who do not have homes of their own.

headline: Government plans to turn One Constitution Avenue building into five-star hotel, says Naqvi
description: Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Wednesday said the government would work to convert the One Constitution Avenue building into a five-star hotel
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Wednesday said the government would work to convert the One Constitution Avenue building into a five-star hotel within the next few months, aiming to address Islamabad’s shortage of hotel accommodation and settle outstanding payments in accordance with the Joint Investigation Team (JIT) report approved by the federal cabinet.

Naqvi said the government also intended to tackle illegal land occupation and encroachments across Islamabad, regardless of their size or location. He noted that the scale of encroachment on public land in the capital was greater than many people realised.

Citing examples from residential sectors, the minister said the CDA chairman had recently informed him about houses in F-6, F-7 and F-8 where residents had extended their lawns beyond their legally approved boundaries.

He urged property owners to remove such extensions and ensure their properties remained within the permitted limits, whether they were located in F-6, F-10 or any other part of the city.

Speaking about One Constitution Avenue, Naqvi said the building had initially been designed as a hotel. With Islamabad facing a shortage of hotel facilities, he said the government would seek an agreement with a major hotel chain to turn the property into a five-star establishment at the earliest.

The minister appreciated the CDA team for pursuing the matter, particularly the authority’s lawyer, Kashif. However, he acknowledged that mistakes by CDA officials had contributed to the situation, adding that the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) would provide further information about those responsible.

Naqvi said the government would pay the concerned parties their outstanding amounts in line with the JIT's findings. He maintained that since the federal cabinet had approved the report, its recommendations were binding and would be implemented accordingly.

He also thanked the prime minister for supporting the process. Recalling an earlier attempt by authorities to take possession of the building, Naqvi said the situation had become difficult and that he was disappointed the following day when the episode was portrayed as though the government had committed a crime.

According to the minister, the prime minister had assured him and other officials that the matter would be decided on merit. He said the premier had directed that there should be no preferential treatment for the wealthy and that the same rules must apply to everyone.

Naqvi further said the JIT report had confirmed the dissolution of the committee formed by the concerned individuals. In line with the cabinet's directions, the CDA Member Administration would assume immediate responsibility for all matters relating to the building.

He said the government's priority was to make the property operational as soon as possible and add a new five-star hotel to Islamabad's hospitality sector.

headline: Top officials blame others over allegations of illegal transfer of 36 acres land in Muzaffargarh
description: MUZAFFARGARH - A land dispute involving 36 acres in Mauza Khanpur Shumali, near Adda Mushtaqabad, has taken a fresh turn, with allegations of an illegal land
author: Khurram Malaizai
article_text: MUZAFFARGARH - A land dispute involving 36 acres in Mauza Khanpur Shumali, near Adda Mushtaqabad, has taken a fresh turn, with allegations of an illegal land transfer, unlawful occupation and apparent buck-passing among government officials. Video allegedly showing police personnel in the company of members of a suspected land-grabbing group has already surfaced, raising serious questions about the role of law enforcement authorities. Meanwhile, a separate video concerning the alleged response of Assistant Commissioner Muzaffar-garh, Umm-e-Habiba, during a recent site visit is expected to be released soon, according to those in-volved in the dispute. The controversy intensified after District Police Officer Muzaffargarh Syed Ghazanfar Ali Shah report-edly attributed responsibility for the matter to the Assistant Commissioner following the circulation of the police video. During her visit to the disputed site, AC Umm-e-Habiba allegedly shifted responsibil-ity to subordinate staff, according to claims made by the affected parties. At the centre of the controversy is the alleged fraudulent transfer (intiqal) of 36 acres of land. The matter is reportedly pending before a civil court, while the property is also said to have been pledged as collateral with a bank. More troubling are claims by the complainants that the original owners died approximately 15 years ago, yet the inheritance of the property has reportedly not been transferred to their legal heirs. This raises fundamental questions about the legal basis on which the disputed land transfer was processed and whose authority was used in the process. Several questions now demand answers. Were the administrative powers of the Assistant Commis-sioner allegedly exercised by private or unauthorised individuals? If the AC was unaware of the dis-puted transfer, who processed or approved it? Who verified the revenue record and inheritance doc-uments before the transfer was sanctioned? And, most importantly, who is allegedly backing the group accused of occupying the land? The controversy has triggered concern among local residents, who have called on Punjab Chief Minis-ter Maryam Nawaz Sharif to take immediate notice of the allegations and order an independent, high-level inquiry. They have also demanded that any public official, government employee or private indi-vidual found involved in misuse of authority, manipulation of revenue records or unlawful occupation of the property should face legal action without discrimination. Those raising the allegations have announced that a video showing AC Muzaffargarh Umm-e-Habiba’s alleged statement and position on the disputed land transfer will be released soon. The recording is expected to provide further insight into the officials’ respective positions and the circumstances sur-rounding the controversy. However, the allegations have yet to be independently verified, and the position of the officials con-cerned, along with the relevant revenue and court records, remains crucial to establishing the facts.

Meanwhile, a separate video concerning the alleged response of Assistant Commissioner Muzaffar-garh, Umm-e-Habiba, during a recent site visit is expected to be released soon, according to those in-volved in the dispute.

The controversy intensified after District Police Officer Muzaffargarh Syed Ghazanfar Ali Shah report-edly attributed responsibility for the matter to the Assistant Commissioner following the circulation of the police video. During her visit to the disputed site, AC Umm-e-Habiba allegedly shifted responsibil-ity to subordinate staff, according to claims made by the affected parties. At the centre of the controversy is the alleged fraudulent transfer (intiqal) of 36 acres of land. The matter is reportedly pending before a civil court, while the property is also said to have been pledged as collateral with a bank.

More troubling are claims by the complainants that the original owners died approximately 15 years ago, yet the inheritance of the property has reportedly not been transferred to their legal heirs. This raises fundamental questions about the legal basis on which the disputed land transfer was processed and whose authority was used in the process.

Several questions now demand answers. Were the administrative powers of the Assistant Commis-sioner allegedly exercised by private or unauthorised individuals? If the AC was unaware of the dis-puted transfer, who processed or approved it? Who verified the revenue record and inheritance doc-uments before the transfer was sanctioned? And, most importantly, who is allegedly backing the group accused of occupying the land?

The controversy has triggered concern among local residents, who have called on Punjab Chief Minis-ter Maryam Nawaz Sharif to take immediate notice of the allegations and order an independent, high-level inquiry. They have also demanded that any public official, government employee or private indi-vidual found involved in misuse of authority, manipulation of revenue records or unlawful occupation of the property should face legal action without discrimination.

Those raising the allegations have announced that a video showing AC Muzaffargarh Umm-e-Habiba’s alleged statement and position on the disputed land transfer will be released soon. The recording is expected to provide further insight into the officials’ respective positions and the circumstances sur-rounding the controversy. However, the allegations have yet to be independently verified, and the position of the officials con-cerned, along with the relevant revenue and court records, remains crucial to establishing the facts.
